Asynchronous request/response state handle used by libcoap to manage delayed (separate) responses. The concrete struct layout is not defined in this header (opaque type). Instances are created by coap_register_async(), updated/triggered via coap_async_set_delay() and coap_async_trigger(), and released with coap_free_async(). Application data can be associated via coap_async_set_app_data2()/coap_async_get_app_data(). Details of fields and lifetime are managed by the library.
Represents the parsed fields of a CoAP Block1/Block2 option (RFC 7959): block number, the More (M) bit, and size exponent (SZX). Used to read/write block options and manage blockwise transfers.

Extended block option representation with BERT (Blockwise Transfer with larger payload, RFC 8323/Q-Block). Tracks normal SZX, augmented size (ASZX) including BERT support, flags indicating if a block is defined and whether BERT mode is active, and the effective chunk size.

struct coap_dtls_pki_t {
  uint8_t version; /** Set to COAP_DTLS_PKI_SETUP_VERSION
                       to support this version of the struct */

  /* Options to enable different TLS functionality in libcoap */
  uint8_t verify_peer_cert;        /**< 1 if peer cert is to be verified */
  uint8_t check_common_ca;         /**< 1 if peer cert is to be signed by
                                    * the same CA as the local cert */
  uint8_t allow_self_signed;       /**< 1 if self-signed certs are allowed.
                                    *     Ignored if check_common_ca set */
  uint8_t allow_expired_certs;     /**< 1 if expired certs are allowed */
  uint8_t cert_chain_validation;   /**< 1 if to check cert_chain_verify_depth */
  uint8_t cert_chain_verify_depth; /**< recommended depth is 3 */
  uint8_t check_cert_revocation;   /**< 1 if revocation checks wanted */
  uint8_t allow_no_crl;            /**< 1 ignore if CRL not there */
  uint8_t allow_expired_crl;       /**< 1 if expired crl is allowed */
  uint8_t allow_bad_md_hash;      /**< 1 if unsupported MD hashes are allowed */
  uint8_t allow_short_rsa_length; /**< 1 if small RSA keysizes are allowed */
  uint8_t is_rpk_not_cert;        /**< 1 is RPK instead of Public Certificate.
                                   *     If set, PKI key format type cannot be
                                   *     COAP_PKI_KEY_PEM */
  uint8_t use_cid;                 /**< 1 if DTLS Connection ID is to be
                                    *     used (Client only, server always enabled)
                                    *     if supported */
  uint8_t reserved[2];             /**< Reserved - must be set to 0 for
                                        future compatibility */

  /** CN check callback function.
   * If not NULL, is called when the TLS connection has passed the configured
   * TLS options above for the application to verify if the CN is valid.
   */
  coap_dtls_cn_callback_t validate_cn_call_back;
  void *cn_call_back_arg;  /**< Passed in to the CN callback function */

  /** SNI check callback function.
   * If not @p NULL, called if the SNI is not previously seen and prior to
   * sending a certificate set back to the client so that the appropriate
   * certificate set can be used based on the requesting SNI.
   */
  coap_dtls_pki_sni_callback_t validate_sni_call_back;
  void *sni_call_back_arg;  /**< Passed in to the sni callback function */

  /** Additional Security callback handler that is invoked when libcoap has
   * done the standard, defined validation checks at the TLS level,
   * If not @p NULL, called from within the TLS Client Hello connection
   * setup.
   */
  coap_dtls_security_setup_t additional_tls_setup_call_back;

  char *client_sni;    /**<  If not NULL, SNI to use in client TLS setup.
                             Owned by the client app and must remain valid
                             during the call to coap_new_client_session_pki().
                             Note: Ignored if literal IPv4 or IPv6 address. */

  coap_dtls_key_t pki_key;  /**< PKI key definition */
};

  COAP_RESPONSE_CODE_HOP_LIMIT_REACHED          = COAP_RESPONSE_CODE(508),

  COAP_SIGNALING_CODE_CSM                       = COAP_SIGNALING_CSM,
  COAP_SIGNALING_CODE_PING                      = COAP_SIGNALING_PING,
  COAP_SIGNALING_CODE_PONG                      = COAP_SIGNALING_PONG,
  COAP_SIGNALING_CODE_RELEASE                   = COAP_SIGNALING_RELEASE,
  COAP_SIGNALING_CODE_ABORT                     = COAP_SIGNALING_ABORT
} coap_pdu_code_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of all PDU codes: request methods, response codes, and signaling codes, using CoAP’s compact numeric encoding macros.

objects.definition: typedef int (*coap_rand_func_t)(void *out, size_t len);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a pseudo-random number generator callback. Implementations must write len bytes of random data into the buffer out and return 1 on success, 0 on failure.

Enumeration of proxy mode and option bit flags for libcoap proxy behavior. Includes deprecated legacy values and newer bit-mapped values for reverse, forward-static, and forward-dynamic proxies, plus STRIP and MCAST option bits.
Describes a single upstream server target for proxying, including destination URI and optional security configurations (DTLS PKI, DTLS PSK, OSCORE).

objects.definition:
typedef struct coap_proxy_server_list_t {
  coap_proxy_server_t *entry; /**< Set of servers to connect to */
  size_t entry_count;         /**< The number of servers in entry list */
  size_t next_entry;          /**< Next server to use (% entry_count) */
  coap_proxy_t type;          /**< The proxy type and option controlling bits
                                   (if old type used, will get mapped into new + bits */
  int track_client_session;   /**< If 1, track individual connections to upstream
                                   server, else 0 for all clients to be multiplexed
                                   over the same upstream session */
  unsigned int idle_timeout_secs; /**< Proxy upstream session idle timeout
                                       (0 is no timeout). Timeout is ignored
                                       if there are any active upstream Observe
                                       requests */
} coap_proxy_server_list_t;
objects.description: A configuration block holding one or more upstream servers and proxy behavior. Supports simple load-balancing via next_entry, proxy type flags, per-client tracking, and idle timeout for upstream sessions.

objects.definition:
typedef coap_pdu_t *(*coap_proxy_response_handler_t)(coap_session_t *session,
                                                     const coap_pdu_t *sent,
                                                     coap_pdu_t *received,
                                                     coap_cache_key_t *cache_key);
objects.description: Function pointer type for proxy response callbacks invoked when a response is received or fetched from cache. Returns the PDU to send back to the client or NULL on error. The handler may replace or take ownership of the received PDU per documentation.

Pointer-to-function type for request method handlers. Implementations receive the target resource, session, incoming request PDU, optional query string, and a pre-populated response PDU to fill in. Exact types referenced (coap_resource_t, coap_session_t, etc.) are declared elsewhere in the library.

objects.definition: typedef void (*coap_resource_release_userdata_handler_t)(void *user_data);
objects.description: Pointer-to-function type for callbacks invoked to release resource user_data when a resource is deleted. Receives the user_data pointer previously associated with a resource.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t coap_print_status_t;
objects.description: Status word type used by printing functions to encode both a 28-bit output length and 4 bits of status flags (e.g., error or truncation). Macros COAP_PRINT_STATUS_* interpret this value.

Fixed-point number used where floating point is avoided. Represents value as integer_part + fractional_part/1000 with 3 decimal digits of precision. Used for timing and rate parameters in session congestion control APIs.
Enumeration of CoAP session roles/type: none, client, server, or temporary server-side HELLO used during DTLS/TLS handshakes.
Enumeration of CoAP session connection state machine phases: none, connecting, (D)TLS handshake, CSM (for reliable transports), established.

objects.definition: typedef void (*coap_app_data_free_callback_t)(void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for freeing application-specific data attached to sessions or endpoints. Called with the stored data pointer when the owning object is deleted.

Heap-allocated mutable string container used by libcoap. Holds byte length and a writable buffer pointer. The buffer is expected to be at least length bytes and typically NUL-terminated when used as text. Create with coap_new_string() and free with coap_delete_string().
Immutable string view/container for read-only byte data. Length plus const data pointer. Typically constructed by copying input data. Free with coap_delete_str_const().
Mutable binary data container. Holds length and writable buffer pointer. Allocate with coap_new_binary(), optionally resize with coap_resize_binary(), and free with coap_delete_binary().
Immutable binary data container for read-only bytes. Construct with coap_new_bin_const() and free with coap_delete_bin_const().

Union wrapper providing dual typed pointers to character data: const char* and const uint8_t*. Useful for APIs that accept either textual or raw byte pointers without casting. No dedicated constructors or destructors; typically stack-allocated or embedded.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*coap_observe_added_t)(coap_session_t *session,
                                    coap_subscription_t *observe_key,
                                    coap_proto_t e_proto,
                                    coap_address_t *e_listen_addr,
                                    coap_addr_tuple_t *s_addr_info,
                                    coap_bin_const_t *raw_packet,
                                    coap_bin_const_t *oscore_info,
                                    void *user_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked when a new observe subscription is established. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Parameters provide session, subscription handle, protocol, endpoint listen address, session address tuple, raw L7 packet, optional OSCORE info, and user data. Destruction/ownership semantics are not described in this header.
Function pointer type for a callback invoked when an observe subscription is being removed. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Parameters provide the session, the subscription handle, and user data.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*coap_track_observe_value_t)(coap_context_t *context,
                                          coap_str_const_t *resource_name,
                                          uint32_t observe_num,
                                          void *user_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked periodically (per save_freq) when an unsolicited observe response is sent, allowing tracking of the current observe number for a resource. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

objects.definition:
typedef int (*coap_dyn_resource_added_t)(coap_session_t *session,
                                         coap_str_const_t *resource_name,
                                         coap_bin_const_t *raw_packet,
                                         void *user_data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked when a dynamic resource is created (e.g., via unknown resource handling). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Provides session, resource path, raw L7 packet, and user data.
Function pointer type for a callback invoked when a resource is removed. Also implies removal of any tracked dynamic resources and observe value tracking. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t coap_tick_t;
objects.description: Internal timer tick type used when WITH_LWIP is defined. Resolution is COAP_TICKS_PER_SECOND (1000 on lwIP).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t coap_time_t;
objects.description: CoAP wallclock time (seconds) on lwIP builds. Derived from ticks via coap_ticks_to_rt().

objects.definition: typedef int32_t coap_tick_diff_t;
objects.description: Signed difference type for comparing two coap_tick_t values on lwIP builds; must be same width considerations as coap_tick_t to allow wrapping semantics.

objects.definition: typedef clock_time_t coap_tick_t;
objects.description: Internal timer tick type when WITH_CONTIKI is defined; aliases Contiki clock_time_t with resolution CLOCK_SECOND.

objects.definition: typedef clock_time_t coap_time_t;
objects.description: CoAP wallclock time (seconds) for Contiki builds; same underlying type as coap_tick_t.

objects.definition: typedef int coap_tick_diff_t;
objects.description: Signed difference type for Contiki builds; must be same size as coap_tick_t to allow wrapping.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t coap_tick_t;
objects.description: Internal timer tick type when RIOT_VERSION is defined; uses microsecond-resolution ticks (XTIMER).

objects.definition: typedef int64_t coap_tick_diff_t;
objects.description: Signed difference type for RIOT builds to compare coap_tick_t values safely across wraparound.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t coap_time_t;
objects.description: CoAP wallclock time in seconds for RIOT builds.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t coap_tick_t;
objects.description: Internal timer tick type for default (POSIX-like) builds; ms resolution with COAP_TICKS_PER_SECOND = 1000.

objects.definition: typedef time_t coap_time_t;
objects.description: CoAP time in seconds since epoch for default (POSIX-like) builds.

objects.definition: typedef int64_t coap_tick_diff_t;
objects.description: Signed difference type for default builds; intended to be same width semantics as coap_tick_t for wraparound-safe comparisons.

objects.definition:
typedef enum coap_uri_scheme_t {
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_COAP = 0,
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_COAPS,     /* 1 */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_COAP_TCP,  /* 2 */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_COAPS_TCP, /* 3 */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_HTTP,      /* 4 Proxy-Uri only */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_HTTPS,     /* 5 Proxy-Uri only */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_COAP_WS,   /* 6 */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_COAPS_WS,  /* 7 */
  COAP_URI_SCHEME_LAST       /* 8 Size of scheme */
} coap_uri_scheme_t;
objects.description: Enumeration of URI scheme identifiers used by libcoap. Even values are non-secure, odd values are secure (mask 0x01). Includes CoAP over UDP/TCP, secure variants, HTTP(S) for proxy use, and WebSocket variants.

Parsed CoAP/HTTP-style URI container holding host, port (host byte order), full path and query strings (as coap_str_const_t slices), and the scheme (coap_uri_scheme_t). host/path/query point to external memory that must remain valid for the lifetime of the coap_uri_t unless created/cloned by the provided constructors.

There are no custom data types defined in this header. It only declares a function coap_ws_set_host_request that references external types coap_session_t and coap_str_const_t, which are not defined here. As a placeholder to fulfill the required schema, this entry notes the absence of defined types.

functions.name: coap_startup
functions.description: Initializes libcoap’s process-wide/platform-specific state before other libcoap APIs are used. Typical usage is to call this once early in program startup (e.g., before creating contexts or sockets) and pair it with coap_cleanup() at program shutdown. Details of what is initialized are not documented here; based on common library patterns, this likely includes platform networking setup (e.g., Winsock on Windows). No return value or error reporting is provided; failure modes (if any) are unknown.
requirements: Call before invoking other libcoap functions that rely on global/platform initialization (inferred from naming and typical library patterns).
Intended to be called once per process lifetime and paired with coap_cleanup() (inferred; exact multiplicity not documented).
No arguments; there are no input constraints.
The function does not report errors (void return); callers cannot detect initialization failure from this API (inferred).

functions.name: coap_cleanup
functions.description: Shuts down and releases libcoap’s process-wide/platform-specific resources previously set up by coap_startup(). Typical usage is to call this once at program shutdown after all libcoap activity has completed. No return value or error reporting is provided; what is cleaned up exactly is not specified in this header.
requirements: Call after all libcoap usage has finished and after a prior coap_startup() (inferred from naming and typical library patterns).
Intended to be called once per process lifetime corresponding to a prior coap_startup() (inferred; exact multiplicity not documented).
No arguments; there are no input constraints.
The function does not report errors (void return); callers cannot detect cleanup failure from this API (inferred).

functions.name: coap_address_get_port
functions.description: Returns the UDP/TCP port associated with the provided network address in host byte order. Inline platform-specific definitions exist, but the interface is uniform. Use to read the bound/target port of a coap_address_t.
requirements: addr must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.
Returned port is in host byte order.

functions.name: coap_address_set_port
functions.description: Sets the port of the provided network address. The port value is specified in host byte order. Inline platform-specific definitions exist, but the interface is uniform.
requirements: addr must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.
port must be provided in host byte order.

functions.name: coap_address_equals
functions.description: Compares two network address objects for equality. Returns 1 if equal, 0 otherwise. Inline platform-specific implementations may assert on NULL.
requirements: a must be non-NULL.
b must be non-NULL.
Both addresses must be valid and initialized.

functions.name: coap_get_available_scheme_hint_bits
functions.signature: uint32_t coap_get_available_scheme_hint_bits(int have_pki_psk, int ws_check, coap_proto_t use_unix_proto);
functions.description: Determines which CoAP protocol schemes are available for a server, returning a bitmask suitable for use as scheme_hint_bits in coap_resolve_address_info(). Intended to guide address resolution for PSK/PKI and WebSockets availability as well as Unix-domain protocol selection.
requirements: have_pki_psk should be 0 or 1 (0 = no PSK/PKI info, 1 = PSK/PKI available).
ws_check should be 0 or 1 (1 = include WebSockets schemes).
use_unix_proto must be set to the appropriate Unix-domain protocol to consider, or COAP_PROTO_NONE to select only INET/INET6 sockets.

functions.name: coap_resolve_address_info
functions.signature: coap_addr_info_t *coap_resolve_address_info(const coap_str_const_t *address, uint16_t port, uint16_t secure_port, uint16_t ws_port, uint16_t ws_secure_port, int ai_hints_flags, int scheme_hint_bits, coap_resolve_type_t type);
functions.description: Resolves the textual address/name into one or more concrete coap_address_t endpoints (linked via coap_addr_info_t) that can be used for bind() (local) or connect() (remote), based on provided ports, getaddrinfo AI_* hint flags, scheme bitmask, and resolve type.
requirements: address must be a valid pointer to a coap_str_const_t containing the address/name to resolve.
port, secure_port, ws_port, and ws_secure_port are port numbers in host byte order for their respective schemes.
ai_hints_flags should be a combination of getaddrinfo AI_* flags appropriate for the lookup.
scheme_hint_bits must be one or more COAP_URI_SCHEME_*_BIT flags OR’d together indicating which schemes to include.
type must be COAP_RESOLVE_TYPE_LOCAL (for bind) or COAP_RESOLVE_TYPE_REMOTE (for connect).
On success, the returned list must be freed by the caller using coap_free_address_info().
Returns NULL on error.

functions.name: coap_free_address_info
functions.description: Frees a chain of coap_addr_info_t entries previously returned by coap_resolve_address_info(), releasing all associated resources.
requirements: info_list may be NULL (no-op) or a pointer previously returned by coap_resolve_address_info().
Each returned list from coap_resolve_address_info() should be freed exactly once.

functions.name: coap_address_init
functions.description: Initializes/resets a coap_address_t to default values. The size field must be set by the caller to indicate the available storage for the underlying sockaddr prior to calling.
requirements: addr must be a non-NULL pointer to a coap_address_t.
Before calling, addr->size must be initialized to the available size for storing addresses (i.e., the capacity of the addr union).

functions.name: coap_address_set_unix_domain
functions.description: Parses a Unix domain socket host component from a CoAP URI, decoding %2F into '/' and populates addr accordingly. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: addr must be a non-NULL pointer to a coap_address_t to be updated.
host must point to the parsed host bytes of the URI; host_len must be the length of that data.
The decoded path must fit within the Unix domain path capacity (implementation-limited by COAP_UNIX_PATH_MAX).
Caller should check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: coap_address_copy
functions.description: Copies a coap_address_t from src to dst. On some platforms this is an inline memcpy; on others it’s provided as a function. Intended to duplicate address structures safely.
requirements: dst must be a non-NULL pointer to writable coap_address_t.
src must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.
After copying, dst contains a complete duplicate of src.

functions.name: coap_address_isany
functions.description: Checks whether the address denotes the wildcard/any-address. Returns 1 if it is the wildcard address, 0 otherwise. Implementation is platform-specific via _coap_address_isany_impl().
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.

functions.name: coap_is_mcast
functions.description: Determines whether the address is a multicast address. Returns 1 if multicast, 0 otherwise. Provided as a normal function on most platforms and as a static inline wrapper on certain embedded platforms.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.

functions.name: coap_is_bcast
functions.description: Determines whether the address is a broadcast address. Returns 1 if broadcast, 0 otherwise. Only available on non-CONTIKI and non-RIOT builds.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.
Function availability may depend on build configuration (not provided for CONTIKI/RIOT).

functions.name: coap_is_af_unix
functions.description: Checks whether the address is an AF_UNIX (Unix domain) address. Returns 1 if AF_UNIX, 0 otherwise. On certain embedded platforms (CONTIKI/RIOT), this always returns 0.
requirements: a must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized coap_address_t.
Behavior may vary by platform; on CONTIKI/RIOT it always returns 0.

functions.name: coap_register_async
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_async_t *coap_register_async(coap_session_t *session, const coap_pdu_t *request, coap_tick_t delay);
functions.description: Allocates and registers a new coap_async_t associated with the given session and request, scheduling a delayed ("separate") response. Returns the registered async handle or NULL on error (including if an async with the same identifier is already registered). On expiry of the delay, a copy of the request is dispatched to the appropriate request handler. Use when a request cannot be answered immediately and a separate response is needed.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer used for asynchronous transmissions.
request must be a valid pointer to the original request PDU to be handled asynchronously.
delay defines when the async triggers; 0 means wait indefinitely (no automatic trigger).
Call may return NULL if allocation fails or if an object with the same identifier is already registered; callers must check for NULL before use.
Do not register a duplicate async with the same identifier (token) as an existing one.

functions.name: coap_async_set_delay
functions.description: Updates the timeout of an existing registered async, changing when it will trigger. On expiry of the new delay, a copy of the original request is sent to the appropriate handler.
requirements: async must be a valid pointer to a previously registered coap_async_t object.
delay is the new delay; 0 means wait indefinitely (no automatic trigger).

functions.name: coap_async_trigger
functions.description: Immediately triggers the registered async so that a copy of the original request is sent to the appropriate handler.
requirements: async must be a valid pointer to a previously registered coap_async_t object.

functions.name: coap_free_async
functions.description: Releases the memory/resources allocated for the async object previously created by coap_register_async, removing it from tracking in the associated session.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer for asynchronous transmissions (typically the one associated with async).
async must be a valid pointer previously obtained via coap_register_async.
Caller must not use async after this call (dangling pointer).

functions.name: coap_find_async
functions.description: Looks up a registered async by token within the given session and returns it if found, or NULL if not found.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t used for asynchronous transmissions.
token must be the PDU token identifying the async to retrieve.
Caller must check for a NULL return to handle "not found".

functions.name: coap_async_set_app_data
functions.description: Deprecated. Sets (overwrites) the application data pointer stored in the async object.
requirements: async must be a valid pointer to a coap_async_t object.
app_data is an opaque pointer managed by the application.
Prefer using coap_async_set_app_data2() instead, as this API is deprecated.

functions.name: coap_async_get_app_data
functions.description: Returns the application data pointer currently stored in the async object.
requirements: async must be a valid pointer to a coap_async_t object (may be const).

functions.name: coap_async_set_app_data2
functions.description: Stores an application data pointer in the async object, optionally with a release callback to be invoked when the async is removed. Returns the previously stored data pointer (if any). The caller is responsible for freeing any returned previous data as appropriate.
requirements: async_entry must be a valid pointer to a coap_async_t object.
data may be NULL to clear previously stored data.
callback may be NULL; if provided, it will be used to release data when the async is removed.
Caller must handle and free (as appropriate) the returned previous data pointer.

functions.name: coap_opt_block_num
functions.description: Extracts and returns the Block option’s num field from the provided option. Use on a Block1 or Block2 option to get the current block number.
requirements: block_opt must point to a valid, initialized coap_opt_t that encodes a Block1 or Block2 option.
block_opt must not be NULL.
The option must contain a parsable Block option; otherwise the returned value is unspecified.

functions.name: coap_more_blocks
functions.signature: COAP_STATIC_INLINE int coap_more_blocks(size_t data_len, unsigned int num, uint16_t szx);
functions.description: Computes whether more than num blocks are needed to transfer data_len bytes when using a block size of 1 << (szx + 4). Returns non-zero if another block is required.
requirements: szx should be a valid SZX value (0–6) as per RFC 7959.
num is the zero-based current block number.
data_len is the total payload size in bytes.

functions.name: coap_get_block
functions.signature: int coap_get_block(const coap_pdu_t *pdu, coap_option_num_t number, coap_block_t *block);
functions.description: Searches pdu for the specified Block option (Block1 or Block2). If found, initializes block with the option values and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.
requirements: number must be COAP_OPTION_BLOCK1 or COAP_OPTION_BLOCK2.
pdu must be a valid, initialized PDU containing options.
block must be a valid, writable pointer; contents are set only on success.
Returns 1 on success, 0 if the option is absent.

functions.name: coap_get_block_b
functions.signature: int coap_get_block_b(const coap_session_t *session, const coap_pdu_t *pdu, coap_option_num_t number, coap_block_b_t *block);
functions.description: Like coap_get_block(), but populates a coap_block_b_t, abstracting BERT details as appropriate for the session. Returns 1 if the Block option is found; 0 otherwise.
requirements: number must be COAP_OPTION_BLOCK1 or COAP_OPTION_BLOCK2.
session must be a valid session associated with pdu.
pdu must be a valid, initialized PDU containing options.
block must be a valid, writable pointer; contents are set only on success.
Returns 1 on success, 0 if the option is absent.

functions.name: coap_write_block_opt
functions.signature: int coap_write_block_opt(coap_block_t *block, coap_option_num_t number, coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t data_length);
functions.description: Writes a Block1 or Block2 option to pdu based on block and the available space, potentially reducing the requested block size (except possibly for the final block). May modify block to reflect what is written. Intended to be called before adding payload data_length bytes (via coap_add_block()).
requirements: number must be COAP_OPTION_BLOCK1 or COAP_OPTION_BLOCK2.
pdu must be a valid, mutable PDU with sufficient option space.
block must be valid and may be modified by this function to the actual values used.
data_length is the length of data that will be added to pdu after this call.
No more options should be added to pdu after this function returns.
Returns 1 on success, negative on error.

functions.name: coap_write_block_b_opt
functions.signature: int coap_write_block_b_opt(coap_session_t *session, coap_block_b_t *block, coap_option_num_t number, coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t data_length);
functions.description: Writes a Block1 or Block2 option (with BERT-aware handling) to pdu using the session context. May reduce the requested block size to fit and updates block to reflect the values actually written.
requirements: number must be COAP_OPTION_BLOCK1 or COAP_OPTION_BLOCK2.
session must be a valid CoAP session.
pdu must be a valid, mutable PDU with sufficient option space.
block must be valid and may be modified by this function to the actual values used.
data_length is the length of data that will be added to pdu after this call.
No more options should be added to pdu after this function returns.
Returns 1 on success, negative on error.

functions.name: coap_add_block
functions.signature: int coap_add_block(coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t len, const uint8_t *data, unsigned int block_num, unsigned char block_szx);
functions.description: Adds the specified block (block number block_num, size 1 << (block_szx + 4)) from the source buffer data to pdu’s payload.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, mutable PDU ready to accept payload data.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
block_szx must be a valid encoded size (typically 0–6).
block_num is the zero-based block index to extract from data.
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: coap_add_block_b_data
functions.signature: int coap_add_block_b_data(coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t len, const uint8_t *data, coap_block_b_t *block);
functions.description: Adds the appropriate portion of data (respecting block->num/size and possible BERT) to pdu’s payload.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, mutable PDU ready to accept payload data.
data must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
block must be a valid pointer containing the current block selection (may include BERT parameters).
Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: coap_block_build_body
functions.signature: coap_binary_t *coap_block_build_body(coap_binary_t *body_data, size_t length, const uint8_t *data, size_t offset, size_t total);
functions.description: Reassembles incoming payload chunks into a single body buffer, inserting length bytes from data at byte offset offset in a representation with estimated total size total. Returns the current body buffer, or NULL on error (and frees body_data).
requirements: body_data must be either NULL (first chunk) or an existing coap_binary_t returned by previous calls.
data must point to length bytes of payload to be inserted at offset.
offset specifies the start position within the full body; must be within or extend the current accumulation in a way acceptable to the implementation.
total is the estimated total size of the complete body.
On error, the function returns NULL and de-allocates body_data; callers must not use the old body_data pointer afterward.

functions.name: coap_add_data_blocked_response
functions.signature: void coap_add_data_blocked_response(const coap_pdu_t *request, coap_pdu_t *response, uint16_t media_type, int maxage, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Server-side helper for request handlers that adds the appropriate part of a response body to response depending on Block2 negotiation. If the body spans multiple blocks, it adds the proper block and an ETag of the entire body and may send the PDU as needed.
requirements: Intended to be called from a server request handler.
request must be the original request PDU; response must be a valid, mutable response PDU.
media_type is the Content-Format value for the payload.
maxage is the Max-Age in seconds; use -1 for no Max-Age.
length is the total size of the full response body; data points to the entire body if available.
The function may process per-block; applications may be called repeatedly for large bodies.
Consider using coap_add_data_response_large() when appropriate (per note).

functions.name: coap_add_data_large_request
functions.signature: COAP_API int coap_add_data_large_request(coap_session_t *session, coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t length, const uint8_t *data, coap_release_large_data_t release_func, void *app_ptr);
functions.description: Associates a large request body buffer with pdu for client-side transmission. If it fits in one PDU, it behaves like coap_add_data() (with optional release callback after transmission). If multiple PDUs are needed, the library handles (Q-)Block1/Size1/Request-Tag and transmits blocks automatically; release_func is called after completion or failure.
requirements: Must be used for a client request PDU.
Fails if data has already been added to pdu.
Must be called exactly once per PDU and be the last modification to pdu before transmission (coap_send()).
COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP must be enabled via coap_context_set_block_mode() for library-managed block transfers.
Application must not modify the contents of data until the transfer completes.
No need for the application to add a (Q-)Block1 option; the library does this.
On completion (or failure), release_func (if not NULL) is called with app_ptr to allow de-allocation.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: coap_add_data_large_request_app
functions.signature: COAP_API int coap_add_data_large_request_app(coap_session_t *session, coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t length, coap_release_large_data_t release_func, coap_get_large_data_t get_func, void *app_ptr);
functions.description: Associates a callback-driven large request body with pdu for client-side transmission. The library performs (Q-)Block1 transfers and calls get_func to fetch each block’s data before sending. release_func is called after completion or failure.
requirements: Must be used for a client request PDU.
Fails if data has already been added to pdu.
Must be called exactly once per PDU and be the last modification to pdu before transmission (coap_send()).
COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP must be enabled via coap_context_set_block_mode() for library-managed block transfers.
No need for the application to add a (Q-)Block1 option; the library does this.
get_func must provide up to max bytes starting at offset into data, and must set *length to the number of bytes provided; *length must equal max for all but the final block.
On completion (or failure), release_func (if not NULL) is called with app_ptr to allow cleanup.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: coap_add_data_large_response
functions.signature: COAP_API int coap_add_data_large_response(coap_resource_t *resource, coap_session_t *session, const coap_pdu_t *request, coap_pdu_t *response, const coap_string_t *query, uint16_t media_type, int maxage, uint64_t etag, size_t length, const uint8_t *data, coap_release_large_data_t release_func, void *app_ptr);
functions.description: Server-side helper for request handlers to attach a (potentially large) response body to response. For single-PDU bodies it behaves like coap_add_data() (adding Content-Format/Max-Age/ETag as appropriate). For multi-PDU bodies it manages (Q-)Block2/Size2/ETag and transmits the segments automatically; release_func is called after completion or failure.
requirements: Used by a server request handler to create a response PDU.
Fails if data has already been added to response.
Must be called exactly once per response PDU and be the last modification before returning from the handler.
COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP must be enabled via coap_context_set_block_mode() for library-managed block transfers.
The application must not modify data until the transfer completes.
No need for the application to add a (Q-)Block2 option; the library does this.
maxage is the Max-Age in seconds; use -1 for no Max-Age.
If etag is non-zero, it is used as the ETag value.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: coap_context_set_block_mode
functions.description: Sets the context-level block transfer handling flags (RFC 7959, Q-Block, etc.). These flags propagate to sessions when created; features may be disabled if a peer does not support them, and further constrained at receive contexts.
requirements: Must be called before any session is set up for the context.
block_mode is a bitwise OR of COAP_BLOCK_* flags defined by the library.
If not set, applications are responsible for manual block handling; COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP enables library-managed transfers.

functions.name: coap_context_set_max_block_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum block size the server supports for Block1/Block2 when sending or receiving. The value propagates to new sessions.
requirements: Must be called before any session is set up for the context.
max_block_size may be 0 to reset, or must be one of: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024.
For the library to manage this, COAP_BLOCK_USE_LIBCOAP must be enabled using coap_context_set_block_mode().
Returns an int status (non-zero success or library-defined).

functions.name: coap_cache_derive_key
functions.description: Derives a cache-key for a given CoAP PDU, optionally incorporating the session when session_based is COAP_CACHE_IS_SESSION_BASED. Global option-ignoring rules (set via coap_cache_ignore_options) are applied during key derivation. Caller must delete the returned key when finished.
requirements: session must be non-NULL if session_based is COAP_CACHE_IS_SESSION_BASED.
pdu must be a valid pointer to a CoAP PDU.
The returned coap_cache_key_t* must be freed by calling coap_delete_cache_key().
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: coap_cache_derive_key_w_ignore
functions.signature:
coap_cache_key_t *coap_cache_derive_key_w_ignore(const coap_session_t *session,
                                                 const coap_pdu_t *pdu,
                                                 coap_cache_session_based_t session_based,
                                                 const uint16_t *ignore_options,
                                                 size_t ignore_count);
functions.description: Derives a cache-key for a given CoAP PDU, optionally incorporating the session, while ignoring a caller-specified set of CoAP option numbers during key calculation. This per-call ignore list overrides the global ignore settings for this derivation only. Caller must delete the returned key.
requirements: session must be non-NULL if session_based is COAP_CACHE_IS_SESSION_BASED.
pdu must be a valid pointer to a CoAP PDU.
If ignore_count > 0, ignore_options must point to at least ignore_count entries.
The returned coap_cache_key_t* must be freed by calling coap_delete_cache_key().
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: coap_delete_cache_key
functions.description: Deletes and frees a cache-key previously created by one of the coap_cache_derive_key functions.
requirements: cache_key should be a pointer previously returned by coap_cache_derive_key or coap_cache_derive_key_w_ignore and not already freed.
Behavior for NULL is not documented; pass a valid cache_key.

functions.name: coap_cache_ignore_options
functions.signature:
COAP_API int coap_cache_ignore_options(coap_context_t *context,
                                       const uint16_t *options, size_t count);
functions.description: Sets, on the given context, which CoAP option numbers are ignored when calculating cache-keys. Options defined as Non-Cache and Observe are always ignored independent of this setting. Passing count = 0 resets the ignore list.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
If count > 0, options must point to an array with at least count entries.
Caller must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: coap_new_cache_entry
functions.signature:
COAP_API coap_cache_entry_t *coap_new_cache_entry(coap_session_t *session,
                                                  const coap_pdu_t *pdu,
                                                  coap_cache_record_pdu_t record_pdu,
                                                  coap_cache_session_based_t session_based,
                                                  unsigned int idle_time);
functions.description: Creates a new cache-entry keyed from the provided PDU and inserts it into the context’s cache hash. If session_based is set, the entry will be deleted when the session is freed. If record_pdu is set, a copy of the PDU is stored and later freed with the cache-entry. idle_time controls expiration (0 means no expiration).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t (used to derive the context and optionally for session-based lifetime).
pdu must be a valid CoAP request PDU used to generate the cache-key.
If record_pdu is COAP_CACHE_RECORD_PDU, the function will retain a copy of the PDU; ensure the PDU is well-formed.
If session_based is COAP_CACHE_IS_SESSION_BASED, the cache-entry is associated with the session and will be deleted when the session is freed.
idle_time is specified in seconds; if 0, the entry does not expire by time.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: coap_delete_cache_entry
functions.description: Removes a cache-entry from the context’s cache and frees associated resources except for any application data. App data is only freed if a release callback was associated with it by the relevant setter.
requirements: context must be the coap_context_t associated with the cache-entry.
cache_entry must be a valid pointer to a cache-entry currently in the cache.
App-specific data stored without a release callback will not be freed by this call; the caller is responsible for cleanup as appropriate.

functions.name: coap_cache_get_by_key
functions.description: Looks up and returns the cache-entry associated with the given cache-key in the specified context. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
cache_key must be a valid cache-key previously derived for this context.
Caller must handle a NULL return (not found).

functions.name: coap_cache_get_by_pdu
functions.description: Looks up and returns the cache-entry corresponding to the provided PDU (and optionally the session if session_based is set). Returns NULL if no matching entry exists.
requirements: session must be valid; required if session_based is COAP_CACHE_IS_SESSION_BASED.
pdu must be the CoAP request PDU to search for.
Caller must handle a NULL return (not found).

functions.name: coap_cache_get_pdu
functions.description: Returns the stored PDU from a cache-entry, if the PDU was recorded at creation time (record_pdu). Returns NULL if no PDU was recorded.
requirements: cache_entry must be a valid pointer to a cache-entry.
PDU will be NULL if the cache-entry was not created with COAP_CACHE_RECORD_PDU.

functions.name: coap_cache_set_app_data
functions.description: Deprecated. Associates application-specific data and an optional free callback with a cache-entry, overwriting any previously stored data. The data must remain valid for the lifetime of the cache-entry unless a callback is provided to release it on deletion.
requirements: cache_entry must be a valid pointer to a cache-entry.
data must be valid for the lifetime of the cache-entry unless a callback is provided.
callback, if non-NULL, will be invoked to free the data when the cache-entry is deleted.
Existing stored data (and its callback) will be replaced/overwritten by this call.

functions.name: coap_cache_set_app_data2
functions.description: Associates application-specific data and an optional release callback with a cache-entry, returning any previously stored data pointer. Passing data = NULL clears previously stored data without setting new data. The caller is responsible for freeing any returned previous data as appropriate.
requirements: cache_entry must be a valid pointer to a cache-entry.
If data is non-NULL and a callback is provided, the callback will be used to release this data when the cache-entry is removed; otherwise the data must remain valid or be managed by the caller.
If data is NULL, the function clears the stored data and returns the previous pointer for the caller to handle.

functions.name: coap_cache_get_app_data
functions.description: Returns the application-specific data currently associated with a cache-entry, or NULL if none was stored.
requirements: cache_entry must be a valid pointer to a cache-entry.
Caller must handle a NULL return when no data is stored.

functions.name: coap_get_log_level
functions.description: Returns the current global CoAP logging level as a COAP_LOG_* value. Use to gate log output or inspect configuration.

functions.name: coap_set_log_level
functions.description: Sets the global CoAP logging level. Messages at or below this level will be emitted by coap_log().
requirements: level must be a valid COAP_LOG_* value.

functions.name: coap_dtls_set_log_level
functions.description: Sets the (D)TLS-specific logging level used by coap_dtls_log().
requirements: level must be a valid COAP_LOG_* value.

functions.name: coap_dtls_get_log_level
functions.description: Returns the current (D)TLS logging level as a COAP_LOG_* value.

functions.name: coap_log_level_desc
functions.description: Returns a human-readable ASCII description string for the provided logging level.
requirements: level should be a valid COAP_LOG_* value.

functions.name: coap_set_log_handler
functions.description: Installs a custom logging callback used for both CoAP and (D)TLS logging. Pass NULL to restore the default handler.
requirements: handler, if non-NULL, must match type void (*)(coap_log_t level, const char *message).
handler must remain valid for the lifetime it is used (no dangling pointers).

functions.name: coap_package_name
functions.description: Returns the library package name as a zero-terminated string.

functions.name: coap_package_version
functions.description: Returns the library version string as a zero-terminated string.

functions.name: coap_package_build
functions.description: Returns the library build identifier as a zero-terminated string.

functions.name: coap_log_impl
functions.description: Internal printf-style logging function used by coap_log()/coap_dtls_log(). Writes to COAP_ERR_FD (for level <= COAP_LOG_CRIT) or COAP_DEBUG_FD (for level >= COAP_LOG_ERR) when allowed by the configured log level. On GCC, it is annotated with format(printf,2,3).
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the provided variadic arguments.
Calls should ensure level is a valid COAP_LOG_* value.
May be called only when appropriate according to log gating (typically via coap_log()/coap_dtls_log()).

functions.name: coap_set_show_pdu_output
functions.description: Selects the output mechanism used by coap_show_pdu(): fprintf() (1, default) or coap_log() (0).
requirements: use_fprintf must be 0 to use coap_log() or 1 to use fprintf().

functions.name: coap_enable_pdu_data_output
functions.description: Enables (1, default) or disables (0) inclusion of PDU data payload in coap_show_pdu() output.
requirements: enable_data must be 0 or 1.

functions.name: coap_show_pdu
functions.description: Pretty-prints the contents of the given PDU at the specified minimum logging level. Output method and data detail depend on coap_set_show_pdu_output() and coap_enable_pdu_data_output().
requirements: pdu must be a valid, initialized coap_pdu_t pointer.
level should be a valid COAP_LOG_* value.
Behavior depends on previously set coap_set_show_pdu_output() and coap_enable_pdu_data_output() settings.

functions.name: coap_show_tls_version
functions.description: Logs the (D)TLS library version information at the specified minimum logging level.
requirements: level should be a valid COAP_LOG_* value.

functions.name: coap_string_tls_version
functions.description: Writes a textual description of the linked/built (D)TLS library version into buffer and returns buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid writable pointer.
bufsize must reflect the writable size of buffer and should be large enough to hold the resulting string (content may be truncated if too small).

functions.name: coap_string_tls_support
functions.description: Writes a textual description of the available (D)TLS library support into buffer and returns buffer.
requirements: buffer must be a valid writable pointer.
bufsize must reflect the writable size of buffer and should be large enough to hold the resulting string (content may be truncated if too small).

functions.name: coap_print_addr
functions.signature: size_t coap_print_addr(const coap_address_t *address, unsigned char *buffer, size_t size);
functions.description: Formats a network address into the provided buffer. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: address must be a valid, initialized coap_address_t pointer.
buffer must be a valid writable pointer.
size specifies the capacity of buffer; output may be truncated to fit.

functions.name: coap_print_ip_addr
functions.signature: const char *coap_print_ip_addr(const coap_address_t *address, char *buffer, size_t size);
functions.description: Formats the IP portion of an address into the provided buffer and returns buffer. As much of the IP address as fits is written.
requirements: address must be a valid, initialized coap_address_t pointer.
buffer must be a valid writable pointer.
size specifies the capacity of buffer; output may be truncated to fit.

functions.name: coap_debug_set_packet_loss
functions.description: Configures simulated packet loss for testing. Accepts either a percentage (0%–100%) or a comma-separated list of packet numbers/ranges to drop. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: loss_level must be a zero-terminated string in one of the supported formats: a percentage (e.g., "0%".."100%") or a comma-separated list of numbers/ranges (e.g., "1,3-5,10").

functions.name: coap_tls_engine_configure
functions.description: Configure an ENGINE for the underlying TLS library using an in-memory configuration block. Currently only OpenSSL is supported. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Intended for applications that need to set up a TLS ENGINE before DTLS/TLS operations in libcoap.
requirements: Only supported with the OpenSSL TLS backend (other TLS libraries are not supported).
The conf_mem pointer must reference a valid, initialized coap_str_const_t containing the ENGINE configuration in memory (exact format/content is library-specific and not specified here).
The function’s success must be checked by its return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure.
Lifetime/ownership of conf_mem is not transferred; the header does not specify ownership, so callers must manage it.

functions.name: coap_tls_engine_remove
functions.description: Remove a previously configured TLS ENGINE from the TLS library. Currently only OpenSSL is supported. This cleanup is automatically performed when coap_free_context() is called; call this explicitly only if you need to remove the ENGINE earlier. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: Only relevant for the OpenSSL TLS backend.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure.
It is not required to call this if coap_free_context() will be invoked, as removal is done automatically.

functions.name: coap_get_tls_library_version
functions.description: Retrieve information about the underlying (D)TLS library in use, including runtime version, library type, and the version libcoap was built against. Returns a pointer to a coap_tls_version_t structure.
requirements: The caller must treat the returned pointer as library-managed; ownership and lifetime are not specified in the header (do not free unless explicitly documented elsewhere).
Return value should be checked for NULL if the caller depends on the information.

functions.name: coap_fls
functions.description: Find-last-set (FLS) bit helper, mirroring the BSD fls() API. Returns the index of the most significant set bit in i, or 0 if i is 0. Intended as a portability shim when the platform does not provide fls(). Details (exact index base and return for 0) are inferred from standard fls semantics; the header provides no further documentation.
requirements: i can be any unsigned int value.
Behavior for i == 0 is inferred to return 0 (standard fls convention); exact indexing semantics are not explicitly documented in this header.

functions.name: coap_flsll
functions.description: Find-last-set (FLS) bit helper for 64-bit (or long long) values, mirroring BSD flsll(). Returns the index of the most significant set bit in i, or 0 if i is 0. Intended as a portability shim when the platform does not provide flsll(). Details (exact index base and return for 0) are inferred from standard flsll semantics; the header provides no further documentation.
requirements: i can be any long long value.
Behavior for i == 0 is inferred to return 0 (standard flsll convention); exact indexing semantics are not explicitly documented in this header.

functions.name: coap_decode_var_bytes
functions.signature: unsigned int coap_decode_var_bytes(const uint8_t *buf, size_t length);
functions.description: Decode a CoAP variable-length byte sequence (big-endian per CoAP option/value conventions) from buf into an up-to-32-bit unsigned integer. Returns the decoded value; for length==0 this will be 0. Intended for decoding CoAP option values and similar var-bytes fields up to 4 bytes wide.
requirements: buf must point to at least length readable bytes when length > 0; buf may be NULL only if length == 0.
length must be in the range [0, 4]; the function only decodes up to 4 bytes (implied by documentation: "Returns the up to 4 byte decoded value").
Input is interpreted as a multi-byte unsigned integer in network byte order (CoAP var-bytes; endianness not explicitly stated here but standard for CoAP).

functions.name: coap_decode_var_bytes8
functions.description: Decode a CoAP variable-length byte sequence (big-endian per CoAP conventions) from buf into an up-to-64-bit unsigned integer. Returns the decoded value; for length==0 this will be 0. Intended for decoding CoAP fields up to 8 bytes wide.
requirements: buf must point to at least length readable bytes when length > 0; buf may be NULL only if length == 0.
length must be in the range [0, 8]; the function only decodes up to 8 bytes (implied by documentation: "Returns the up to 8 byte decoded value").
Input is interpreted as a multi-byte unsigned integer in network byte order (CoAP var-bytes; endianness not explicitly stated here but standard for CoAP).

functions.name: coap_encode_var_safe
functions.signature: unsigned int coap_encode_var_safe(uint8_t *buf, size_t length, unsigned int value);
functions.description: Encode a 32-bit value into a CoAP variable-length byte sequence in buf. Uses up to 4 bytes as needed. Returns the number of bytes used, or 0 on error. May legitimately return 0 bytes when encoding a value of 0. Callers should prefer this safe variant as it bounds writes by the provided output length.
requirements: buf must point to at least length writable bytes.
length must be sufficient to hold the encoded form of value (0–4 bytes). If insufficient, the function returns 0 (error).
value must fit in 32 bits (type is unsigned int).
The function may return 0 either because value==0 (encoded length 0) or due to error (e.g., insufficient length); callers should distinguish this case according to their protocol needs.

functions.name: coap_encode_var_safe8
functions.signature: unsigned int coap_encode_var_safe8(uint8_t *buf, size_t length, uint64_t value);
functions.description: Encode a 64-bit value into a CoAP variable-length byte sequence in buf. Uses up to 8 bytes as needed. Returns the number of bytes used, or 0 on error. May legitimately return 0 bytes when encoding a value of 0.
requirements: buf must point to at least length writable bytes.
length must be sufficient to hold the encoded form of value (0–8 bytes). If insufficient, the function returns 0 (error).
value is any 64-bit unsigned integer.
The function may return 0 either because value==0 (encoded length 0) or due to error (e.g., insufficient length); callers should distinguish this case according to their protocol needs.

functions.name: coap_encode_var_bytes
functions.signature: COAP_STATIC_INLINE COAP_DEPRECATED int coap_encode_var_bytes(uint8_t *buf, unsigned int value);
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper maintained for backward compatibility. Encodes value into a CoAP variable-length byte sequence, but internally assumes the output buffer has 4 bytes available (passes sizeof(value) as the buffer length), which can overflow a smaller caller-provided buffer. Prefer coap_encode_var_safe(). Returns the number of bytes used or 0 on error (or 0 when encoding value 0).
requirements: Deprecated: callers should migrate to coap_encode_var_safe().
If used, buf must point to at least 4 writable bytes; otherwise memory beyond buf may be overwritten (as the function passes length=4 to coap_encode_var_safe regardless of the actual buffer size).
value must fit in 32 bits (type is unsigned int).
Return value 0 is ambiguous between encoding value 0 and an error; callers must handle accordingly.

functions.name: coap_register_event_handler
functions.description: Registers or de-registers an application-provided event callback for a CoAP context. Passing a non-NULL hnd installs that handler and overwrites any previously registered handler; passing NULL removes any existing handler. The handler will be invoked by libcoap when events (DTLS/TCP/CSM/session/message/OSCORE/WebSocket/keepalive/reconnect) occur, typically from the CoAP I/O loop.
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t pointer obtained from libcoap.
hnd may be NULL to de-register the current handler; otherwise it must be a function matching coap_event_handler_t (int (*)(coap_session_t *session, const coap_event_t event)).
Only one handler is active per context; registering a new handler replaces the previous one.
The supplied handler should return 0 (no further action) or 1 (reserved for future use) as documented for coap_event_handler_t.

functions.name: coap_set_event_handler
functions.description: Deprecated alias of coap_register_event_handler(). Registers an event callback for the given CoAP context, replacing any previously registered handler. Prefer coap_register_event_handler(); to clear a handler, call coap_register_event_handler(context, NULL).
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t pointer obtained from libcoap.
hnd should be a function matching coap_event_handler_t (int (*)(coap_session_t *session, const coap_event_t event)).
Behavior for hnd == NULL is not documented here; use coap_register_event_handler(context, NULL) to de-register.
The supplied handler should return 0 (no further action) or 1 (reserved for future use) as documented for coap_event_handler_t.
Function is deprecated; new code should call coap_register_event_handler().

functions.name: coap_clear_event_handler
functions.description: Deprecated helper that clears the event handler registered with the given CoAP context. Prefer coap_register_event_handler(context, NULL).
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t pointer obtained from libcoap.
Function is deprecated; new code should call coap_register_event_handler(context, NULL).

functions.name: coap_socket_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing a socket-related error. Typical usage is to obtain an explanatory message after a network I/O operation fails, similar to strerror() for socket errors. The exact error source and lifetime/thread-safety of the returned string are not documented here and are therefore unknown.
requirements: The returned string is read-only; the caller must not modify it (const char *).
The caller must not attempt to free the returned pointer; ownership remains with the library (inferred from return type and common patterns).
For meaningful output, call this function in the context of handling a socket/network I/O error (inferred from the function name and common library patterns).

functions.name: coap_memory_init
functions.description: Initializes libcoap’s memory management layer. On constrained devices this must be called before using coap_malloc()/typed allocators. In lwIP + custom pools builds it is a no-op (lwIP must already be initialized).
requirements: Call once before using coap_malloc()/coap_malloc_type() on constrained devices (as documented).
In lwIP + custom pools builds, ensure lwIP is fully initialized before libcoap becomes active (per header comment).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown from this header.

functions.name: coap_malloc_type
functions.description: Allocates size bytes from libcoap’s typed memory pools. The type selects the storage bucket on constrained devices. Memory allocated here must be released using coap_free_type() with the same type. Returns NULL on error. In lwIP + custom pools builds this maps to a fixed-size pool allocator and fails if size exceeds the pool’s object size.
requirements: type must be a valid coap_memory_tag_t value that corresponds to the object being allocated.
size is the number of bytes requested; allocation may return NULL on failure.
The returned pointer must be freed with coap_free_type(type, ptr) using the same type tag.
In lwIP + custom pools builds, allocation fails if size is larger than the configured pool element size for that type (per macro check).

functions.name: coap_realloc_type
functions.description: Reallocates a block previously obtained from coap_malloc_type() or coap_realloc_type() to size bytes and returns the new pointer. Only COAP_STRING type is supported. On error, NULL is returned and the original pointer p must be freed separately with coap_free_type(). In lwIP + custom pools builds, if p is non-NULL the call returns p when the new size still fits the fixed pool element; otherwise NULL; if p is NULL it behaves like coap_malloc_type().
requirements: type must be COAP_STRING (only supported type, per documentation).
p must be a pointer previously allocated by coap_malloc_type() or coap_realloc_type() with the same type.
On failure, the function returns NULL and the caller must explicitly free p using coap_free_type(type, p).

In lwIP + custom pools builds: if p != NULL and size exceeds the pool element size, the call returns NULL (no reallocation to a larger pool occurs); if p == NULL, the call behaves like coap_malloc_type(type, size).

functions.name: coap_free_type
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated with coap_malloc_type() (or coap_realloc_type()). The type must match the type used at allocation time.
requirements: p must be a pointer obtained from coap_malloc_type() or coap_realloc_type().
type must be the same coap_memory_tag_t used when the memory was allocated.
Behavior for p == NULL is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: coap_dump_memory_type_counts
functions.description: Dumps current usage counts of typed allocations to the libcoap log at the provided level. Only available/meaningful when COAP_MEMORY_TYPE_TRACK is defined to 1. In lwIP + custom pools builds this maps to coap_lwip_dump_memory_pools().
requirements: COAP_MEMORY_TYPE_TRACK must be defined to 1 for tracking data to be available (per documentation).
log_level must be a valid coap_log_t logging level.
Logging subsystem must be initialized before calling (implied by use of logging; specifics unknown).

functions.name: coap_malloc
functions.description: Backward-compatibility wrapper for coap_malloc_type() using the COAP_STRING type. Returns NULL on error. In lwIP + custom pools builds, this function must not be used and triggers an assertion.
requirements: Use only in builds that are not lwIP + custom pools; in lwIP builds it must not be used (asserts).
The returned pointer must be freed with coap_free().
size is the number of bytes requested; may return NULL on failure.

functions.name: coap_free
functions.description: Backward-compatibility wrapper for coap_free_type() using the COAP_STRING type. In lwIP + custom pools builds, this function must not be used and triggers an assertion.
requirements: Use only in builds that are not lwIP + custom pools; in lwIP builds it must not be used (asserts).
object must have been allocated by coap_malloc() (or otherwise be a COAP_STRING allocation).
Behavior for object == NULL is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: coap_register_response_handler
functions.description: Registers a response callback on the given CoAP context. The handler is invoked whenever a response PDU is received on any session bound to this context.
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t pointer.
handler may be NULL to clear a previously registered handler.
The registered handler must be re-entrant or otherwise safe for the library's calling context.

functions.name: coap_register_nack_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a confirmable message is dropped after retries, an RST is received, or a network/TLS-level event prevents delivery.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
handler may be NULL to clear a previously registered handler.

functions.name: coap_register_ping_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a CoAP Ping message is received on any session for the context.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
handler may be NULL to clear a previously registered handler.

functions.name: coap_register_pong_handler
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when a CoAP Pong message is received on any session for the context.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
handler may be NULL to clear a previously registered handler.

functions.name: coap_register_dynamic_resource_handler
functions.description: Installs a handler to dynamically create resources when unknown resources are requested. Limits the number of concurrently created dynamic resources.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
create_handler must be non-NULL to enable dynamic creation; pass NULL to disable.
dynamic_max is the maximum concurrent dynamic resources; 0 means unlimited.
The create_handler must return a valid coap_resource_t* or NULL on error.
The handler is not required to be thread-safe due to internal serialization described.

functions.name: coap_register_block_data_handler
functions.description: Registers a handler invoked for each received block during block-wise transfers when COAP_BLOCK_SINGLE_BODY is enabled. For clients it is called for each block; for servers only for resources flagged with COAP_RESOURCE_USE_BLOCK_DATA_HANDLER; not called for proxy sessions.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
handler may be NULL to clear the handler.
Effective only when COAP_BLOCK_SINGLE_BODY is enabled at build/config time.
For server usage, target resources must be created with COAP_RESOURCE_USE_BLOCK_DATA_HANDLER flag set.

functions.name: coap_register_option
functions.description: Registers a non-standard (non-RFC) option number with the context so libcoap ignores it for unknown/critical/duplicate/reserved checks when sending/receiving PDUs.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
number must be an option not defined by CoAP RFCs; registering standard options is not intended.

functions.name: coap_new_context
functions.description: Creates a new CoAP context that holds stack state and endpoints, optionally bound to a listening address.
requirements: listen_addr may be NULL or a valid coap_address_t depending on desired binding (details depend on libcoap configuration).
Caller must release the returned context with coap_free_context().

functions.name: coap_context_set_psk
functions.signature:
COAP_API int coap_context_set_psk(coap_context_t *context, const char *hint,
                                  const uint8_t *key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Deprecated: Sets the default server PSK identity hint and key for DTLS/TLS on the context. Use coap_context_set_psk2() instead.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
If hint is NULL, PSK authentication is disabled.
key must be non-NULL and key_len > 0 for authentication to succeed.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: coap_context_set_psk2
functions.description: Sets default server-side PSK parameters using the supplied setup structure (recommended replacement for coap_context_set_psk).
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
setup_data must be non-NULL; if NULL, PSK authentication will fail.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
The fields of coap_dtls_spsk_t must be correctly initialized per libcoap expectations.

functions.name: coap_context_set_pki
functions.description: Sets default server-side PKI (certificate-based) authentication parameters on the context.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
setup_data must be non-NULL; if NULL, PKI authentication will fail.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
Certificates/keys referenced in setup_data must be valid and accessible for the process.

functions.name: coap_context_set_pki_root_cas
functions.description: Sets default root CA trust for client or server by loading PEM-encoded CAs from a file and/or directory.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
ca_file may be NULL or path to a PEM file containing Root CAs.
ca_dir may be NULL or path to a directory containing PEM files with Root CAs.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
Paths provided must be accessible and readable by the process.

functions.name: coap_context_load_pki_trust_store
functions.description: Loads the host's default trusted CA store into the context for use by client or server.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
Availability and content depend on system trust store configuration.

functions.name: coap_context_set_keepalive
functions.description: Configures session keepalive behavior: after the specified idle time, sends Empty (unreliable) or PING (reliable) and considers the session disconnected if no response per protocol rules; 0 disables keepalives.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
seconds is the inactivity period before keepalive; 0 disables.

functions.name: coap_context_set_cid_tuple_change
functions.description: Testing aid: changes the client source port every N packets to exercise Connection ID tuple changes. Returns 1 if supported, else 0.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
every specifies how often to change the source port; interpretation is for testing only.
Returns 1 if CID is supported and change set, else 0.

functions.name: coap_context_set_max_token_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum token size (RFC 8974) the context will use/accept.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
max_token_size must be between 8 and 65804 inclusive (per comment).

functions.name: coap_context_get_coap_fd
functions.description: Returns the internal libcoap file descriptor suitable for integration with select/epoll, or -1 if epoll is not available.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 when epoll is not available on the platform.

functions.name: coap_context_set_max_idle_sessions
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of idle (unused) server sessions retained. If exceeded, the least recently used idle session is removed. 0 disables monitoring (default).
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_get_max_idle_sessions
functions.description: Gets the current maximum number of idle sessions configured for the context.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_session_timeout
functions.description: Sets the inactivity timeout (seconds) after which an unused server session will be closed. 0 means use default (300 seconds).
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_session_reconnect_time
functions.description: Configures the delay (seconds) before attempting to reconnect a failed client session. 0 (default) disables reconnection. Observe subscriptions are automatically restarted on reconnection; dynamically-created resources may need persistence handling.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
reconnect_time is in seconds; 0 disables reconnection.

functions.name: coap_context_set_session_reconnect_time2
functions.description: Like coap_context_set_session_reconnect_time() but also sets the number of reconnection attempts. 0 retries means infinite; maximum 255. Retry counter resets on successful reconnection.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
reconnect_time is in seconds; 0 disables reconnection.
retry_count in range 0..255; 0 means infinite retries.

functions.name: coap_context_get_session_timeout
functions.description: Gets the current session inactivity timeout (seconds).
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_shutdown_no_observe
functions.description: Disables sending Observe 5.03 responses on context shutdown via coap_free_context(). Without calling this, 5.03 messages are sent for each active Observe subscription when freeing the context.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
Call before coap_free_context() to suppress Observe notifications on shutdown.

functions.name: coap_context_set_csm_timeout
functions.description: Deprecated: Sets the CSM negotiation response timeout in seconds for TCP sessions. 0 (default) means wait forever. Use coap_context_set_csm_timeout_ms() instead.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_get_csm_timeout
functions.description: Deprecated: Gets the CSM timeout in seconds. Use coap_context_get_csm_timeout_ms() instead.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_csm_timeout_ms
functions.description: Sets the TCP CSM negotiation response timeout in milliseconds. Initial default is 1000 ms; value may be clamped to approximately 10–10000 ms by the library.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
csm_timeout_ms is in milliseconds; the library may adjust it into the range 10–10000 ms.

functions.name: coap_context_get_csm_timeout_ms
functions.description: Gets the TCP CSM negotiation response timeout in milliseconds.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_csm_max_message_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum message size (CSM max session size) that can be received over (TCP) sessions.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_get_csm_max_message_size
functions.description: Gets the configured CSM maximum message size the context will accept.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_max_handshake_sessions
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of sessions in DTLS/TLS handshake. If exceeded, the least recently used session in handshake is removed. 0 disables monitoring (default).
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_get_max_handshake_sessions
functions.description: Gets the current maximum number of sessions allowed to be in handshake state concurrently.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_new_message_id
functions.description: Returns a new message ID for the session and updates session->tx_mid. Returned in network byte order for easier tracing.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_free_context
functions.description: Frees a CoAP context, clearing queues, deleting registered resources, and freeing attached endpoints.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer or NULL (behavior for NULL is library-defined, typically no-op).
After calling, context and any of its pointers must not be used.

functions.name: coap_set_app_data
functions.description: Deprecated: Stores an application-specific pointer in the context, overwriting any previous value. Use coap_context_set_app_data2() instead.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
data must remain valid for the lifetime of the context.

functions.name: coap_get_app_data
functions.description: Deprecated: Retrieves the application data pointer previously stored with coap_set_app_data(). Returns NULL if none.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_new_error_response
functions.description: Creates a new ACK/error response PDU for the given request and error code, copying selected options per the option filter. Unless built with SHORT_ERROR_RESPONSE, includes a reason phrase payload with Content-Format 0. Caller must free with coap_free().
