requirements: request must be a valid pointer to the received confirmable request PDU.
code must be a valid CoAP response code.
opts may be NULL or a valid filter specifying which options to copy.
Returns NULL on error; on success, caller owns the returned PDU and must free it.

functions.name: coap_send_error
functions.description: Builds and sends an error response for the given request and code, copying options as per filter. Returns the message ID on success or COAP_INVALID_MID on failure.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
request must be a valid pointer to the original request PDU.
code must be a valid CoAP response code.
opts may be NULL or a valid option filter.

functions.name: coap_send_message_type
functions.signature:
COAP_API coap_mid_t coap_send_message_type(coap_session_t *session, const coap_pdu_t *request,
                                           coap_pdu_type_t type);
functions.description: Sends a minimal message (typically ACK or RST) in response to the given request. Returns a valid MID or COAP_INVALID_MID if not sent.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
request must be a valid request PDU to respond to.
type must be a valid coap_pdu_type_t (e.g., ACK or RST).

functions.name: coap_send_ack
functions.description: Sends an empty ACK for the specified request. Returns the message ID on success or COAP_INVALID_MID on error.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
request must be a valid PDU that needs acknowledging.

functions.name: coap_send_rst
functions.description: Sends an empty RST for the specified request. Returns the message ID on success or COAP_INVALID_MID on error.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
request must be a valid PDU to reset.

functions.name: coap_send
functions.description: Sends the given PDU on the session. coap_send() takes ownership and frees the PDU; the caller must not use or free it after calling.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
pdu must be a valid, heap-allocated coap_pdu_t pointer; after calling, it must not be accessed by the caller.
Returns message ID on success or COAP_INVALID_MID on error.

functions.name: coap_send_recv
functions.signature:
COAP_API int coap_send_recv(coap_session_t *session, coap_pdu_t *request_pdu,
                            coap_pdu_t **response_pdu, uint32_t timeout_ms);
functions.description: Sends a request PDU and waits for the response PDU, handling block-wise transfers and Observe per handler configuration. Returns time spent in ms (>=0) on success, or negative error codes per documented list.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
request_pdu must be a valid request PDU; the caller must free it after processing (ownership is NOT transferred here per comment).
response_pdu must be a valid pointer to receive an allocated response PDU pointer when a response is received; the caller must free the response after processing.
timeout_ms must be positive; -1 is returned for invalid timeout.
Caller must handle negative return codes: -2 (transmit fail), -3 (NACK/Event), -4 (I/O error), -5 (timeout), -6 (terminated), -7 (client mode not enabled).

functions.name: coap_send_recv_terminate
functions.description: Terminates any active coap_send_recv() sessions, causing waiting calls to return early.

functions.name: coap_handle_event
functions.description: Invokes the context's event handler for the specified event and session. Returns the handler's result or 0 if none registered.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
event must be a valid coap_event_t value.
session should be the session associated with the event (may be NULL depending on event semantics).

functions.name: coap_can_exit
functions.description: Returns 1 if there are no pending messages to send or dispatch in the context queues; 0 otherwise. Note: 0 does not imply a response has arrived for any outstanding request.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_ticks
functions.description: Writes the current internal tick counter (COAP_TICKS_PER_SECOND ticks per second) into the provided storage.
requirements: Argument must be a non-NULL pointer to coap_tick_t storage.

functions.name: coap_join_mcast_group_intf
functions.signature:
COAP_API int coap_join_mcast_group_intf(coap_context_t *ctx, const char *groupname,
                                        const char *ifname);
functions.description: Joins the specified UDP multicast group for all currently defined UDP endpoints in the context, optionally on a specific interface.
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
groupname must be a valid multicast group name/address string.
ifname may be NULL (let OS choose) or a valid network interface name.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: coap_mcast_set_hops
functions.description: Sets the hop count (TTL) for outgoing multicast traffic on the session. Default is 1 (expires at boundary).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
hops is the TTL value to set (non-negative; typical platform-specific valid ranges apply).
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.

functions.name: coap_mcast_per_resource
functions.description: Enables per-resource multicast request processing, allowing resource-level configuration (via coap_resource_init() flags).
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_app_data
functions.description: Deprecated: Stores an application-specific pointer in the context, overwriting any previous value. Prefer coap_context_set_app_data2().
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_context_set_app_data2
functions.description: Stores an application-specific pointer in the context and returns the previously stored value (if any). Optionally registers a callback to release the data when the context is deleted.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
data may be NULL to clear previous data.
If provided, callback will be invoked on context removal to release the stored data.
Caller is responsible for freeing any previously returned data (if appropriate).

functions.name: coap_context_get_app_data
functions.description: Retrieves application-specific data stored in the context via coap_context_set_app_data() or coap_context_set_app_data2(). Returns NULL if none.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_io_process
functions.description: Performs all pending network I/O and optionally waits for input up to timeout_ms, using select() or epoll depending on build. Returns time spent in ms or -1 on error.
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
timeout_ms can be COAP_IO_WAIT (block until next internal action or packet), COAP_IO_NO_WAIT (return immediately after processing), or a finite millisecond timeout.
Caller must handle -1 return on error.

functions.name: coap_io_process_with_fds
functions.description: Like coap_io_process(), but integrates additional file descriptors into the internal select() loop. Updates the fd_sets to reflect the select() results. Only available when not built for LwIP/RIOT/Contiki.
requirements: Available only if not built with WITH_LWIP, RIOT_VERSION, or WITH_CONTIKI.
ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
timeout_ms semantics as for coap_io_process().
nfds must be the maximum FD set in any of the provided fd_sets plus one.
readfds/writefds/exceptfds may be NULL or point to initialized fd_set structures; they are updated on return.
Returns milliseconds spent or -1 on error.

functions.name: coap_io_pending
functions.description: Checks whether there is any I/O pending for the context (e.g., Observe activity, partial block transfers). Internally may call coap_io_process() to progress I/O.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
Returns 1 if I/O pending, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: coap_io_prepare_io
functions.description: Internal: Determines which sockets want I/O (COAP_SOCKET_WANT_xxx) and populates sockets[] for external select() use. Also transmits timed-out delayed packets and returns the next timeout in ms for select().
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
sockets must be a valid array of coap_socket_t* with capacity max_sockets.
max_sockets is the capacity of sockets[].
num_sockets must be a non-NULL pointer; set to the number of valid entries on output.
now is the current time (ticks).
Returns max milliseconds to wait in select(), or 0 to wait forever.

functions.name: coap_io_do_io
functions.description: Internal: Processes read, write, accept, or connect I/O indicated by COAP_SOCKET_CAN_xxx on sockets associated with the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
now is the current time (ticks).
If epoll support is compiled in, coap_io_do_epoll() must be used instead.

functions.name: coap_io_prepare_epoll
functions.signature: COAP_API unsigned int coap_io_prepare_epoll(coap_context_t *ctx, coap_tick_t now);
functions.description: Internal: Prepares epoll-based I/O by transmitting any timed-out delayed packets and returns the next timeout (ms) to use for epoll_wait().
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
now is the current time (ticks).
Use only when libcoap is compiled with epoll support.

functions.name: coap_io_do_epoll
functions.signature:
COAP_API void coap_io_do_epoll(coap_context_t *ctx, struct epoll_event *events,
                               size_t nevents);
functions.description: Internal: Processes the provided epoll events for the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
events must point to an array of struct epoll_event returned by epoll_wait().
nevents is the number of entries in events.
Use only when libcoap is compiled with epoll support.

functions.name: coap_io_process_loop
functions.signature:
COAP_API int coap_io_process_loop(coap_context_t *context,
                                  coap_io_process_thread_t main_loop_code,
                                  void *main_loop_code_arg, uint32_t timeout_ms,
                                  uint32_t thread_count);
functions.description: Runs coap_io_process() in a loop across up to thread_count threads. The main thread optionally invokes main_loop_code periodically at least every timeout_ms. Use coap_io_process_terminate_loop() to stop.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
main_loop_code may be NULL or a function that must not block.
timeout_ms is the delay parameter used by the main thread between iterations (upper bound).
If multithreading protection is not available, thread_count is ignored and only a single thread runs.
Returns an int status (success/failure semantics are library-defined).

functions.name: coap_io_process_terminate_loop
functions.description: Signals all additional threads created by coap_io_process_loop() to terminate and breaks the main loop so coap_io_process_loop() returns.

functions.name: coap_io_process_configure_threads
functions.description: Configures a set of worker threads to offload coap_io_process() work with load balancing across inactive threads.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
thread_count is the number of threads to configure.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: coap_io_process_remove_threads
functions.description: Releases worker threads previously configured for alternate coap_io_process() handling.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_socket_get_fd
functions.description: Returns the underlying libcoap file descriptor for a socket for use in external event loops, or COAP_INVALID_SOCKET if not applicable on the platform.
requirements: socket must be a valid coap_socket_t pointer.
Caller must handle COAP_INVALID_SOCKET if the platform does not use file descriptors.

functions.name: coap_io_get_fds
functions.signature:
COAP_API unsigned int coap_io_get_fds(coap_context_t *context, coap_fd_t read_fds[],
                                      unsigned int *have_read_fds,
                                      unsigned int max_read_fds,
                                      coap_fd_t write_fds[],
                                      unsigned int *have_write_fds,
                                      unsigned int max_write_fds,
                                      unsigned int *rem_timeout_ms);
functions.description: Retrieves current libcoap file descriptors in read-pending and write-pending states and the remaining timeout until the next internal activity.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
read_fds must point to an array with capacity max_read_fds; have_read_fds must be non-NULL to receive the count.
write_fds must point to an array with capacity max_write_fds; have_write_fds must be non-NULL to receive the count.
rem_timeout_ms must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the remaining timeout.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.

functions.name: coap_socket_get_flags
functions.description: Returns the OR'ed COAP_SOCKET_* flags for the given socket for integration with external event loops.
requirements: socket must be a valid coap_socket_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_socket_set_flags
functions.description: Sets the internal COAP_SOCKET_* flags for the given socket, for use by external event loop integrations.
requirements: socket must be a valid coap_socket_t pointer.
flags should be constructed from valid COAP_SOCKET_* flag bits.

functions.name: coap_lwip_dump_memory_pools
functions.description: For LwIP builds: Dumps the current state of LwIP memory pools at the specified log level. Requires MEMP_STATS=1 and LWIP_STATS_DISPLAY=1 in lwipopts.h.
requirements: Available only when building with LwIP support.
log_level must be a valid coap_log_t level.

functions.name: coap_lwip_set_input_wait_handler
functions.description: For LwIP builds: Sets a wait/timeout callback used by coap_io_process() to block until input or timeout.
requirements: Available only when building with LwIP support.
context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
handler must be a valid function pointer to receive wait notifications.
input_arg is passed to the handler when invoked.

functions.name: coap_opt_parse
functions.signature: size_t coap_opt_parse(const coap_opt_t *opt, size_t length, coap_option_t *result);
functions.description: Parses a single CoAP option at opt into result. Returns the number of bytes consumed from the buffer or 0 on error. Use to decode the option header (delta/length) plus locate the option value within a PDU buffer.
requirements: opt must point to the start of an encoded option within a buffer.
length must be the maximum number of bytes available starting at opt; parsing will not read past opt + length.
result must be a valid, writable pointer; it is filled only if the return value > 0.
Caller must handle a 0 return as an error (illegal delta/length or insufficient bytes).
Option list length check must be done by the caller before using parsing helpers (as noted elsewhere in the iterator init).

functions.name: coap_opt_size
functions.description: Computes the total encoded size in bytes of the option starting at opt (including header and value). Returns 0 on error.
requirements: opt must point to an encoded option or an option jump.
Caller must treat a 0 return as an error; options require at least one byte.

functions.name: coap_option_filter_clear
functions.description: Clears (resets) all entries in an option filter, making it match no options.
requirements: filter must be a valid, writable coap_opt_filter_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_option_filter_set
functions.description: Marks the given option number as enabled in the filter. Returns 1 if set, 0 if the number cannot be represented in the filter.
requirements: filter must be a valid, writable coap_opt_filter_t pointer.
number is a CoAP option number; if it does not fit the filter’s capacity, the function returns 0.
Caller should check the return value to detect lack of space.

functions.name: coap_option_filter_unset
functions.description: Clears the given option number from the filter. Returns 1 if the bit was cleared, 0 if it was not previously set.
requirements: filter must be a valid, writable coap_opt_filter_t pointer.
number is a CoAP option number that may or may not be present in the filter.
Caller should check the return value to know if anything changed.

functions.name: coap_option_filter_get
functions.description: Checks whether the given option number is present in the filter. Returns 1 if present, 0 otherwise.
requirements: filter must be a valid coap_opt_filter_t pointer.
number is a CoAP option number.

functions.name: coap_option_iterator_init
functions.description: Initializes an option iterator to the beginning of pdu’s option list and applies an optional filter. Returns oi on success, NULL on failure (e.g., no options).
requirements: pdu must be a valid coap_pdu_t with an already length-validated option section (caller must perform the length check before calling).
oi must be a valid, writable iterator structure; it will be initialized by this function.
filter may be NULL (COAP_OPT_ALL) to iterate over all options; otherwise only options matching the filter are returned.
Fence-post option numbers (14, 28, 42, …) are always skipped by iteration.

functions.name: coap_option_next
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next option, updating oi, and returns a pointer to the encoded option or NULL if there are no more options.
requirements: oi must have been successfully initialized by coap_option_iterator_init().
If a filter was provided at init time, options not matching the filter are skipped.
Caller must check for NULL to detect end of iteration.
Iterator internal state (e.g., current option number) is updated on each call.

functions.name: coap_check_option
functions.description: Initializes oi to filter for the given option number and returns the first matching option in pdu, or NULL if not found.
requirements: pdu must be a valid coap_pdu_t with a valid option list.
oi must be a valid, writable iterator structure; it will be initialized by this function.
number is the desired CoAP option number to search for.
Caller must check for NULL to handle the not-found case.

functions.name: coap_opt_setheader
functions.signature: size_t coap_opt_setheader(coap_opt_t *opt, size_t maxlen, uint16_t delta, size_t length);
functions.description: Encodes an option header (delta and length fields) into the buffer at opt. Returns the number of bytes used, or 0 on error. The return value indicates by how much to advance opt before writing the option value.
requirements: opt must point to writable buffer space for the encoded header.
maxlen must be the total available space remaining at opt; it must be large enough for the header encoding.
delta must be the desired option delta and length the value length to encode; invalid/unsupported encodings cause a 0 return.
Caller must check for a 0 return before writing the option value.

functions.name: coap_opt_encode_size
functions.description: Computes how many bytes are required to encode an option (header plus value) with the given delta and value length.
requirements: delta and length must reflect the intended option encoding; large values may require extended fields and increase size.
Caller should use this to allocate/verify buffer sizes before encoding.

functions.name: coap_opt_encode
functions.signature: size_t coap_opt_encode(coap_opt_t *opt, size_t n, uint16_t delta, const uint8_t *val, size_t length);
functions.description: Encodes an option (header and value) at opt with the given delta and value bytes. Returns number of bytes written (< n) or 0 on error (e.g., insufficient space).
requirements: opt must point to a writable buffer of at least n bytes.
n must be large enough to hold the encoded header and the value; otherwise the function returns 0.
val must point to at least length bytes (may be NULL only when length is 0).
delta and length must be the desired option delta and value length; invalid encodings cause a 0 return.
Caller must check the return value and must not write past opt + return_value.

functions.name: coap_opt_length
functions.description: Returns the decoded value length of the option at opt. Returns 0 if opt is not a valid option (note: a valid option can also have length 0).
requirements: opt must point to an option jump or the beginning of an encoded option.
Caller must treat a 0 return as either an error or a zero-length option; subsequent logic should verify context.

functions.name: coap_opt_value
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the start of the option’s value for the encoded option at opt, or NULL if opt is invalid.
requirements: opt must point to an option jump or the beginning of an encoded option.
Caller must check for NULL before dereferencing and must use coap_opt_length() to know the value length.

functions.name: coap_new_optlist
functions.signature: coap_optlist_t *coap_new_optlist(uint16_t number, size_t length, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new optlist entry for the given option number and value bytes. On failure returns NULL. For numeric options, callers should strip leading zero bytes (big-endian) using coap_encode_var_safe()/coap_encode_var_safe8() to minimize size and avoid illegal oversize values.
requirements: number must be a valid CoAP option number (COAP_OPTION_*).
data must point to at least length bytes (may be NULL only when length is 0).
Caller must check for NULL and free the returned entry via coap_delete_optlist() (through chain deletion) when no longer needed.
Where applicable, callers should pre-strip leading zeros from big-endian option values to conform to size limits.

functions.name: coap_add_optlist_pdu
functions.description: Sorts the current optlist chain (per RFC 7252 ordering) and adds its options to the given PDU. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, writable coap_pdu_t to which options can be added.
optlist_chain must point to a chain of coap_optlist_t entries (may be NULL or empty).
Caller must check the return value to detect failure.
Function sorts the chain before adding; callers need not pre-sort.

functions.name: coap_insert_optlist
functions.description: Inserts an optlist entry into the chain referenced by optlist_chain. The chain should initially be NULL before the first insertion. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: optlist_chain must be a valid pointer to a chain head; it should be set to NULL before the first insertion.
optlist must be a valid coap_optlist_t pointer created by coap_new_optlist().
Caller must manage the lifetime of the chain and later free it with coap_delete_optlist().
Caller must check the return value to detect insertion failure.

functions.name: coap_delete_optlist
functions.description: Deletes all entries in the optlist chain and frees their memory.
requirements: optlist_chain may be NULL or a valid chain head; after return the chain entries must not be accessed.
Caller must not use freed optlist entries after deletion.

functions.name: coap_option_setb
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper: sets the bit for the given type in the filter. Returns 1 if set, -1 on error. Use coap_option_filter_set() instead.
requirements: filter must be a valid, writable coap_opt_filter_t pointer.
type is a CoAP option number; if it does not fit in the filter, the function returns -1.
Caller should migrate to coap_option_filter_set().

functions.name: coap_option_clrb
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper: clears the bit for the given type in the filter. Returns 1 if cleared, -1 if the bit was not set. Use coap_option_filter_unset() instead.
requirements: filter must be a valid, writable coap_opt_filter_t pointer.
type is a CoAP option number; if the bit is not set, return value is -1.
Caller should migrate to coap_option_filter_unset().

functions.name: coap_option_getb
functions.description: Deprecated wrapper: gets the bit state for the given type in the filter. Returns 1 if set, 0 if not. Use coap_option_filter_get() instead.
requirements: filter must be a valid coap_opt_filter_t pointer.
type is a CoAP option number.
Caller should migrate to coap_option_filter_get().

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_oscore
functions.signature:
COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session_oscore(coap_context_t *ctx,
                                                        const coap_address_t *local_if,
                                                        const coap_address_t *server,
                                                        coap_proto_t proto,
                                                        coap_oscore_conf_t *oscore_conf);
functions.description: Create a new client CoAP session to a designated server with all application data protected using OSCORE (RFC8613). Intended for clients that want an unsecured transport CoAP session whose payloads/options are protected by OSCORE. The provided OSCORE configuration is consumed by this call.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid, initialized coap_context_t.
local_if may be NULL to let the OS choose the local interface; if non-NULL, the port number in the address should be 0 so a free port is auto-selected.
server must reference a valid server address; if the server port is 0, the library will use the protocol’s default port.
proto must be a valid CoAP protocol value supported by the build.
oscore_conf must point to a valid OSCORE configuration; ownership is transferred and the structure is freed by this call (do not use or free it after calling).
On success, the returned coap_session_t must be released by the caller with coap_session_release().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must handle a NULL return.

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_oscore_psk
functions.signature:
COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session_oscore_psk(coap_context_t *ctx,
                                                            const coap_address_t *local_if,
                                                            const coap_address_t *server,
                                                            coap_proto_t proto,
                                                            coap_dtls_cpsk_t *psk_data,
                                                            coap_oscore_conf_t *oscore_conf);
functions.description: Create a new client CoAP session to a designated server that uses DTLS PSK credentials for transport security, while also protecting application data using OSCORE. Use when both DTLS-PSK and OSCORE are required.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid, initialized coap_context_t.
local_if may be NULL; if non-NULL, its port should be 0 to auto-select a free port.
server must reference a valid server address; if the server port is 0, the default port for the protocol is used.
proto must be a valid CoAP protocol value supported by the build.
psk_data must point to valid DTLS PSK parameters (coap_dtls_cpsk_t) expected by libcoap.
oscore_conf must point to a valid OSCORE configuration; ownership is transferred and the structure is freed by this call (do not reuse or free it afterward).
On success, the returned coap_session_t must be released by the caller with coap_session_release().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for and handle a NULL return.

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_oscore_pki
functions.signature:
COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session_oscore_pki(coap_context_t *ctx,
                                                            const coap_address_t *local_if,
                                                            const coap_address_t *server,
                                                            coap_proto_t proto,
                                                            coap_dtls_pki_t *pki_data,
                                                            coap_oscore_conf_t *oscore_conf);
functions.description: Create a new client CoAP session to a designated server that uses DTLS/TLS with PKI credentials for transport security, while also protecting application data using OSCORE. Use when both PKI-based DTLS/TLS and OSCORE are required.
requirements: ctx must reference a valid, initialized coap_context_t.
local_if may be NULL; if non-NULL, its port should be 0 to auto-select a free port.
server must reference a valid server address; if the server port is 0, the protocol’s default port is used.
proto must be a valid CoAP protocol value supported by the build.
pki_data must point to valid PKI parameters (coap_dtls_pki_t) expected by libcoap.
oscore_conf must point to a valid OSCORE configuration; ownership is transferred and the structure is freed by this call (do not reuse or free it afterward).
On success, the returned coap_session_t must be released by the caller with coap_session_release().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for and handle a NULL return.

functions.name: coap_context_oscore_server
functions.description: Set the default OSCORE configuration on a coap_context_t for server-side processing. This config is then used to protect/verify OSCORE for incoming/outgoing messages handled by the context.
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t used for server operations.
oscore_conf must point to a valid OSCORE configuration; ownership is transferred and the structure is freed by this call (do not use or free it afterward).
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: coap_new_oscore_conf
functions.signature:
coap_oscore_conf_t *coap_new_oscore_conf(coap_str_const_t conf_mem,
                                         coap_oscore_save_seq_num_t save_seq_num_func,
                                         void *save_seq_num_func_param,
                                         uint64_t start_seq_num);
functions.description: Parse an OSCORE configuration held in memory and construct a coap_oscore_conf_t to be used for OSCORE operations. The configuration memory contains the OSCORE parameters; an optional callback can be provided to persist the Sender Sequence Number, and a start sequence number can be supplied (e.g., after reboot).
requirements: conf_mem must contain the serialized in-memory OSCORE configuration expected by libcoap (format specifics not provided here).
save_seq_num_func may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must conform to coap_oscore_save_seq_num_t and be safe to call to persist sequence numbers, using save_seq_num_func_param.
start_seq_num should be the stored Sender Sequence Number retrieved from non-volatile memory, or 0 if none.

On success, the returned coap_oscore_conf_t must be freed by the caller with coap_delete_oscore_conf() when no longer required, unless ownership is transferred to libcoap via functions like coap_new_client_session_oscore*() or coap_context_oscore_server().
Returns NULL on failure; callers must check for and handle a NULL return.

functions.name: coap_delete_oscore_conf
functions.description: Release all resources associated with an OSCORE configuration created with coap_new_oscore_conf(), if still owned by the caller. Returns 1 if the configuration was successfully removed, otherwise 0 if not found.
requirements: oscore_conf must be a pointer previously obtained from coap_new_oscore_conf() and still owned by the caller (i.e., not already transferred to libcoap or freed).
Returns 1 on successful removal, 0 if not found; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: coap_new_oscore_recipient
functions.description: Add a specific Recipient ID to the server’s OSCORE context, enabling OSCORE protection for that recipient. Only applicable on the server side. The recipient is added to the OSCORE context that was previously established via coap_new_client_session_oscore*() or coap_context_oscore_server().
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t that already has an OSCORE context configured via coap_new_client_session_oscore*() or coap_context_oscore_server().
recipient_id must point to a valid, constant binary identifier for the recipient.
This function is server-only as per the note in the documentation.
Returns 1 on successful addition, 0 if there is an issue; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: coap_delete_oscore_recipient
functions.description: Remove a specific Recipient ID from the server’s OSCORE context, stopping further OSCORE protection for that recipient. Only applicable on the server side. The removal operates on the OSCORE context first defined via coap_new_client_session_oscore*() or coap_context_oscore_server().
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t that already has an OSCORE context configured via coap_new_client_session_oscore*() or coap_context_oscore_server().
recipient_id must point to the binary Recipient ID to remove.
Returns 1 on successful removal, 0 if not found; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: coap_response_phrase
functions.description: Returns a human-readable, zero-terminated phrase that describes the given CoAP response code. Intended for logging and diagnostics. If SHORT_ERROR_RESPONSE is defined at build time, this function is not available and expands to a NULL-returning macro.
requirements: Available only when SHORT_ERROR_RESPONSE is not defined at compile time; otherwise coap_response_phrase(x) is a macro that always returns NULL.
Argument code must be a CoAP response code value (8-bit); unknown codes will return NULL.
The returned pointer is to static storage; do not free it.

functions.name: coap_pdu_from_pbuf
functions.description: Creates a CoAP PDU from an lwIP pbuf, taking over the pbuf reference. The pbuf content is copied into the new PDU; the pbuf will be freed when the PDU is freed.
requirements: Available only when WITH_LWIP is defined at compile time.
The provided pbuf must be contiguous and have only one reference (as enforced by this function; failures are fatal per comment).
Caller must treat the pbuf reference as transferred to the PDU; do not free the pbuf directly after a successful call.
On success, the returned PDU must be freed with coap_delete_pdu() if not sent via coap_send().

functions.name: coap_pdu_init
functions.signature: coap_pdu_t *coap_pdu_init(coap_pdu_type_t type, coap_pdu_code_t code, coap_mid_t mid, size_t size);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new CoAP PDU with capacity for up to size bytes. Sets the message type, code, and message ID (mid) as provided. Use when you need explicit control of PDU buffer size.
requirements: size specifies the maximum allowed number of bytes for the message; it must be large enough to hold header, token, options, and payload you intend to add.
If mid is unknown/not applicable, pass 0.
If coap_send() is not called with the PDU, the caller must free it with coap_delete_pdu().

functions.name: coap_new_pdu
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_pdu_t *coap_new_pdu(coap_pdu_type_t type, coap_pdu_code_t code, coap_session_t *session);
functions.description: Creates a new skeletal CoAP PDU for the given session with the specified type and code. Lets the library choose appropriate sizing based on the session.
requirements: session must point to a valid, initialized coap_session_t.
If the PDU is not sent via coap_send(), it must be freed by the caller using coap_delete_pdu().

functions.name: coap_delete_pdu
functions.description: Disposes of a CoAP PDU and frees associated storage, decrementing an internal reference count if present.
requirements: Do not call directly for PDUs that have been (or will be) passed to coap_send(), as coap_send() will call coap_delete_pdu() automatically.
For PDUs used with coap_send_recv(), the caller must explicitly delete both sending and receiving PDUs.
Safe to call multiple times; if the PDU has a reference count > 0, only the count is decremented and the PDU may persist.
pdu must be a valid pointer previously obtained from libcoap allocation APIs (e.g., coap_pdu_init, coap_new_pdu, coap_pdu_duplicate, coap_pdu_from_pbuf).

functions.name: coap_pdu_duplicate
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_pdu_t *coap_pdu_duplicate(const coap_pdu_t *old_pdu, coap_session_t *session, size_t token_length, const uint8_t *token, coap_opt_filter_t *drop_options);
functions.description: Creates a duplicate of an existing PDU, optionally omitting specific options. The payload/body data is not copied. Useful for retransmissions or creating related requests/responses with similar options.
requirements: old_pdu must point to a valid, initialized PDU.
session must be a valid, initialized coap_session_t for the new PDU.
If token_length > 0, token must point to at least token_length bytes; the provided token is set on the duplicated PDU.
drop_options may be NULL to copy all options; otherwise it must be a valid option filter indicating options to exclude.
Caller must free the returned PDU with coap_delete_pdu() if not sent.

functions.name: coap_pdu_parse
functions.signature: int coap_pdu_parse(coap_proto_t proto, const uint8_t *data, size_t length, coap_pdu_t *pdu);
functions.description: Parses raw bytes of a CoAP message into the provided PDU structure. The target PDU must have enough space for the token, options, and payload. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error.
requirements: proto must indicate the session protocol used to encode the PDU (e.g., COAP_PROTO_UDP/TCP/TLS/DTLS).
data must point to length bytes of a single complete CoAP message.
pdu must point to a PDU structure that provides sufficient storage for any token, options, and payload contained in data.
On failure, return value is 0 and contents of pdu are unspecified.

functions.name: coap_add_token
functions.signature: int coap_add_token(coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t len, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Adds a token of length len to the PDU. Must be called before adding options or payload. Fails if a token was already added.
requirements: pdu must be valid and modifiable.
Must be called at most once per PDU; calling after a token has already been added will fail.
len and data must describe the complete token; data must point to at least len bytes.
len must fit in the available PDU space and within protocol token length constraints; otherwise the function fails (returns 0).
Must be called before adding options and payload, as per CoAP message layout.

functions.name: coap_add_option
functions.signature: size_t coap_add_option(coap_pdu_t *pdu, coap_option_num_t number, size_t len, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Adds an option with the given number and data to the PDU. Must be called before adding payload. Returns the total encoded option length on success, or 0 on failure.
requirements: pdu must be valid and modifiable.
Must be called before any payload/data has been added to the PDU; if data was already added, this function fails.
number must be a valid CoAP option number.
data must point to at least len bytes; the option value must already be correctly encoded for its option type.
The option must fit within the remaining PDU space; otherwise the function fails and returns 0.

functions.name: coap_add_data
functions.signature: int coap_add_data(coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t len, const uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Appends a payload of length len to the PDU. Must be the first and only payload addition (i.e., fail if payload already present). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: pdu must be valid and modifiable.
Must be called only once; if payload/data has already been added, the function fails.
data must point to at least len bytes to copy.
The payload plus header/options must fit within the PDU capacity.

functions.name: coap_add_data_after
functions.description: Reserves space for payload of length len at the end of the PDU and returns a pointer to where the caller must copy the payload. Must be called before any payload has been added.
requirements: pdu must be valid and modifiable.
Must be called only if no payload/data has yet been added to the PDU; otherwise returns NULL.
len must fit in the remaining PDU capacity; on failure, returns NULL.
Caller must copy exactly len bytes to the returned location before using/sending the PDU.

functions.name: coap_get_data
functions.signature: int coap_get_data(const coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t *len, const uint8_t **data);
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the payload and its length from the PDU. Returns 1 on success, 0 if there is no payload.
requirements: pdu must be a valid PDU containing a payload to succeed.
len and data must be non-NULL pointers to receive outputs.
The returned data pointer becomes invalid when the PDU is destroyed or modified; do not free it.

functions.name: coap_get_data_large
functions.signature: int coap_get_data_large(const coap_pdu_t *pdu, size_t *len, const uint8_t **data, size_t *offset, size_t *total);
functions.description: Retrieves payload information from a PDU, including support for block-wise transfer. Provides the current chunk length and pointer, its offset from the start of the total body, and the total size. Returns 1 on success, 0 if the PDU has no data.
requirements: pdu must be a valid PDU.
len, data, offset, and total must be non-NULL pointers to receive outputs.
The returned data pointer is only valid as long as the PDU remains alive and unmodified; do not free it.
If offset + *len < *total, additional data blocks follow (informational behavior to guide callers).

functions.name: coap_pdu_get_code
functions.description: Returns the CoAP code (method/response/signaling) of the PDU.
requirements: pdu must be a valid pointer to a PDU.

functions.name: coap_pdu_set_code
functions.description: Sets the CoAP code in the PDU to the provided value.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, modifiable PDU.
code must be a valid coap_pdu_code_t value appropriate for the PDU's role (request/response/signaling).

functions.name: coap_pdu_get_type
functions.description: Returns the CoAP message type (CON, NON, ACK, RST) of the PDU.
requirements: pdu must be a valid pointer to a PDU.

functions.name: coap_pdu_set_type
functions.description: Sets the CoAP message type of the PDU to the provided value.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, modifiable PDU.
type must be one of the values from coap_pdu_type_t (COAP_MESSAGE_CON/NON/ACK/RST).

functions.name: coap_pdu_get_token
functions.description: Returns the token associated with the PDU as an immutable binary object.
requirements: pdu must be a valid pointer to a PDU.
The returned token reference becomes invalid when the PDU is destroyed or modified.

functions.name: coap_pdu_get_mid
functions.description: Returns the message ID (MID) of the PDU.
requirements: pdu must be a valid pointer to a PDU.

functions.name: coap_pdu_set_mid
functions.description: Sets the message ID (MID) in the PDU to the provided value.
requirements: pdu must be a valid, modifiable PDU.
mid should be a valid CoAP message ID (0..2^16); pass 0 if unknown/not applicable.

functions.name: coap_set_prng
functions.description: Sets/replaces the library’s default pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) function with the callback provided in rng. The callback must conform to coap_rand_func_t: it fills len bytes into out and returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise. Use this to plug in a custom PRNG before calling functions that require randomness (e.g., coap_prng).
requirements: rng must be a valid function pointer compatible with coap_rand_func_t (int (*)(void *out, size_t len)).
The rng implementation must write exactly len bytes into the buffer pointed to by out when successful.
The rng implementation must return 1 on success and 0 otherwise.
Callers should set the PRNG before invoking routines that rely on random bytes (e.g., before coap_prng), if a custom PRNG is desired.

functions.name: coap_prng_init
functions.description: Seeds the library’s default PRNG with the provided seed. On platforms where getrandom() is available, the seed is ignored and the system RNG is used. Typically called during application initialization when deterministic seeding is desired or required.
requirements: seed is an unsigned int; no specific range restrictions are documented.
Behavior note: if the platform provides getrandom(), the seed parameter is ignored (no effect).
If relying on a seedable PRNG (no getrandom()), invoke this before functions that consume random bytes.

functions.name: coap_prng
functions.description: Fills buf with len bytes of random data using the library’s default PRNG (which can be replaced via coap_set_prng). Returns 1 on success and 0 otherwise. Use for obtaining raw random bytes needed by the library or application.
requirements: buf must point to a writable memory region of at least len bytes.
len specifies the exact number of random bytes to write; large values may fail depending on the PRNG implementation.
Callers must check the return value and handle a 0 (failure) result appropriately.
If a custom PRNG is required, call coap_set_prng beforehand; otherwise the library’s default is used.

functions.name: coap_register_proxy_response_handler
functions.description: Registers a proxy-specific response handler that the proxy logic will invoke whenever a response is received. If no proxy handler is registered, the general response handler set by coap_register_response_handler() is used. Typical usage is to call this once per coap_context_t during initialization to intercept upstream responses processed by the proxy.
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t for which the handler is being installed.
handler must be a valid function matching coap_proxy_response_handler_t (whether NULL is accepted is unknown from this header).
If not set, responses will be dispatched to the handler registered via coap_register_response_handler() (behavioral note).

functions.name: coap_verify_proxy_scheme_supported
functions.description: Checks whether a given CoAP URI scheme is supported for an in-progress proxy connection. Use this to validate that the scheme (e.g., coap, coaps, coap+tcp, etc.) is acceptable before attempting to forward via the proxy.
requirements: scheme must be a valid coap_uri_scheme_t enumerator.
Caller should check the return value: 1 means supported, 0 means not supported.

functions.name: coap_proxy_forward_request
functions.description: Forwards an incoming client request upstream to the next proxy/server, handling reverse, forward-static, or forward-dynamic proxying per server_list and any Proxy-Uri/Proxy-Scheme options. This function is for requests that must be proxied; direct requests to the next hop are not supported via this API (create a separate client session with coap_new_client_session_proxy() for direct traffic). On success returns 1; on failure returns 0 and sets an appropriate response code in the provided response PDU.
requirements: req_session must be a valid client coap_session_t representing the requesting client.
request must be a valid, initialized coap_pdu_t containing the client's request.
response must be a valid, initialized coap_pdu_t that will be populated with a response to send back to the client.
resource must reference the resource associated with this request (valid, initialized coap_resource_t).
cache_key must be either NULL or a cache key generated from the request PDU; if non-NULL, it is used to correlate request/response through the proxy.
server_list must be a valid, initialized coap_proxy_server_list_t describing the upstream target(s).
This function must not be used for requests that should go directly to the next proxy/server; instead, create a new client session using coap_new_client_session_proxy() (limitation).
Caller must check the return value: 1 indicates success, 0 indicates failure (with response PDU code set accordingly).

functions.name: coap_proxy_forward_response
functions.description: Forwards an upstream response PDU back to the appropriate client of the proxy. It updates cache_key to the key originally provided to coap_proxy_forward_request() so the caller can manage its lifetime. Returns COAP_RESPONSE_OK on success or COAP_RESPONSE_FAIL on failure.
requirements: rsp_session must be the valid upstream coap_session_t on which the response was received.
received must be a valid, initialized coap_pdu_t containing the received response.
cache_key must point to a coap_cache_key_t* variable; it will be updated to the cache key pointer associated with the original forwarded request.
The caller should delete the returned cache key unless the original client request established an Observe that will yield unsolicited responses (explicit requirement from documentation).
Caller must handle the return value (one of COAP_RESPONSE_OK or COAP_RESPONSE_FAIL).

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_proxy
functions.description: Creates a new client session that uses the proxy logic to communicate with the defined upstream server(s). If multiple servers are listed, selection may not always be the first entry. Unless coap_send_recv() is used, responses will be delivered to the handler registered via coap_register_response_handler(), not the proxy-specific handler.
requirements: context must be a valid, initialized coap_context_t.
server_list must be a valid, initialized coap_proxy_server_list_t and must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned session (it is used for every coap_send()/coap_send_recv()).
Caller must check the return value: non-NULL indicates success; NULL indicates failure.
On success, the returned session must be released by the caller using coap_session_release().

functions.name: coap_resource_init
functions.description: Create and initialize a new CoAP resource with the provided URI path and behavior flags. The resource can later be registered to a context with coap_add_resource() and have method handlers attached. If COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_RELEASE_URI is set, coap_delete_resource() will free the URI storage as documented.
requirements: uri_path must point to a valid coap_str_const_t describing the resource path; leading '/' is not required (e.g., "full/path/for/resource").

If COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_RELEASE_URI is set in flags and the URI memory is to be freed by libcoap, the coap_str_const_t::s must either point to constant text or to memory owned by the coap_str_const_t object itself (i.e., within the allocated coap_str_const_t).
If COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_CON is not set, notifications default to COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_NON (every 5th notification confirmable).
If COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_NON_ALWAYS is set, observe notifications will always be sent non-confirmable (note the RFC 7641 implications).
flags may include other COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_* as needed (e.g., multicast, OSCORE, FORCE_SINGLE_BODY, etc.).
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_resource_unknown_init
functions.description: Create a resource that handles requests to unknown Uri-Path via a provided PUT handler. Additional method handlers (GET/POST/DELETE, etc.) can be added later. Used to dynamically create or manage resources on first PUT.
requirements: There can be only one unknown resource handler per context; creating a new one overrides any previous unknown handler.
put_handler must be a valid function pointer implementing the PUT behavior for unknown Uri-Path.
It is not possible to observe the unknown resource via GET; if observation is needed, the PUT/POST handler should create a separate observable resource.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_resource_unknown_init2
functions.description: Create a resource to handle unknown Uri-Path with a PUT handler and additional control over multicast request handling via flags. Useful for constrained or group communication scenarios and reverse-proxy forwarding of .well-known/core when COAP_RESOURCE_HANDLE_WELLKNOWN_CORE is set.
requirements: There can be only one unknown or reverse-proxy resource handler per context; attaching a new one overrides the previous definition.
put_handler must be a valid function pointer implementing PUT semantics for unknown Uri-Path.
It is not possible to observe the unknown resource via GET; create a separate resource in the PUT/POST handler to support observe.

flags is zero or more COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_*MCAST* ORed together to control multicast behavior; COAP_RESOURCE_HANDLE_WELLKNOWN_CORE can be used to pass .well-known/core to the unknown handler instead of handling locally.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_resource_proxy_uri_init
functions.signature:
coap_resource_t *coap_resource_proxy_uri_init(coap_method_handler_t handler,
                                              size_t host_name_count, const char *host_name_list[]);
functions.description: Create a resource that handles proxy URIs using a single handler for all request methods (PUT/POST/GET/etc.). The resource recognizes the provided host names as valid proxy identities.
requirements: There can be only one proxy resource handler per context; attaching a new one overrides the previous definition.
handler must be a valid message handler that can process all request types as proxy operations.
host_name_count must be at least 1.
host_name_list must be a valid array of host_name_count C-strings identifying names this proxy is known by.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_resource_proxy_uri_init2
functions.signature:
coap_resource_t *coap_resource_proxy_uri_init2(coap_method_handler_t handler,
                                               size_t host_name_count,
                                               const char *host_name_list[],
                                               int flags);
functions.description: Create a proxy-URI handling resource with a unified handler and explicit multicast control via flags.
requirements: There can be only one proxy resource handler per context; attaching a new one overrides the previous definition.
handler must be a valid function that handles all request methods for proxy operations.
host_name_count must be at least 1.
host_name_list must be a valid array of host_name_count C-strings.
flags is zero or more COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_*MCAST* ORed together to control multicast handling.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_resource_reverse_proxy_init
functions.description: Create a resource for reverse-proxy handling (including .well-known/core) with control over multicast request behavior. The single handler processes all reverse-proxy requests.
requirements: There can be only one reverse-proxy or unknown resource handler per context; attaching a new one overrides the previous definition.
handler must be a valid function pointer that processes all request methods for reverse-proxying.
flags is zero or more COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_*MCAST* ORed together to control multicast handling.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_get_resource_from_uri_path
functions.description: Look up and return the resource associated with the given URI path within the specified context. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t with registered resources.
uri_path must point to a valid coap_str_const_t that uniquely identifies the resource's URI path.
Returns NULL when no matching resource exists; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: coap_resource_get_uri_path
functions.description: Retrieve the URI path associated with a resource, if present.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
Returns NULL if the resource has no URI path; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: coap_resource_set_mode
functions.description: Set the observe notification message type behavior for a resource. Mode must be COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_NON or COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_CON.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
mode must be one of COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_NON or COAP_RESOURCE_FLAGS_NOTIFY_CON.

functions.name: coap_resource_set_userdata
functions.description: Attach an application-defined user_data pointer to a resource for later retrieval in handlers.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
data is stored as-is; memory remains under caller control (library does not copy or manage it unless a release handler is set at the context level).

functions.name: coap_resource_get_userdata
functions.description: Return the user_data pointer previously associated with the resource via coap_resource_set_userdata().
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.

functions.name: coap_resource_release_userdata_handler
functions.description: Define a context-wide callback that is invoked to release the user_data associated with a resource when that resource is deleted.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t.
callback may be NULL to remove/disable the release handler; otherwise it must be a valid function matching coap_resource_release_userdata_handler_t.
The callback is called when a resource is deleted to release its user_data.

functions.name: coap_add_resource
functions.description: Register a previously created resource with a context so it participates in request dispatch and discovery.
requirements: resource must have been created by coap_resource_init() or coap_resource_unknown_init().
context must be a valid coap_context_t into which the resource will be inserted.
The resource’s storage will later be released by coap_delete_resource().

functions.name: coap_delete_resource
functions.description: Remove and free a resource from the context. Returns 1 if the resource was found and destroyed, 0 otherwise. The context parameter is ignored (kept for backward compatibility).
requirements: resource identifies the resource to delete; must be valid if deletion is to succeed.
Return value must be checked: 1 indicates deletion occurred, 0 indicates not found.
context parameter is ignored by the implementation.

functions.name: coap_register_handler
functions.description: Deprecated: register a request handler for a specific method on a resource. Use coap_register_request_handler() instead.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
method must be a valid CoAP request code (e.g., COAP_REQUEST_GET/PUT/POST/DELETE).
handler must be a valid function pointer implementing coap_method_handler_t.

functions.name: coap_register_request_handler
functions.description: Register a request handler for a specific CoAP method on the given resource.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
method must be a valid CoAP request code (e.g., COAP_REQUEST_GET/PUT/POST/DELETE).
handler must be a valid function pointer implementing coap_method_handler_t.

functions.name: coap_add_attr
functions.description: Add a link-format attribute (name and optional value) to a resource. Attribute strings point to the provided coap_str_const_t storage unless flagged for release.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
name must be a valid coap_str_const_t string; value may be NULL if the attribute has no value.
The name/value pointers must remain valid for the lifetime of the attribute unless COAP_ATTR_FLAGS_RELEASE_NAME and/or COAP_ATTR_FLAGS_RELEASE_VALUE are set.

If COAP_ATTR_FLAGS_RELEASE_NAME or COAP_ATTR_FLAGS_RELEASE_VALUE is set so that libcoap frees the string on attribute deletion, the coap_str_const_t::s must either point to constant text or to data within the allocated coap_str_const_t parameter itself.
Returns NULL on error; callers must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: coap_find_attr
functions.description: Find the first attribute on a resource matching the provided name.
requirements: resource must be a valid coap_resource_t.
name must be a valid coap_str_const_t representing the attribute name to search for.
Returns NULL if no attribute is found; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: coap_attr_get_value
functions.description: Return the value string for the given attribute, or NULL if none.
requirements: attribute must be a valid coap_attr_t.
Returns NULL if the attribute has no value; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: coap_print_link
functions.signature:
coap_print_status_t coap_print_link(const coap_resource_t *resource,
                                    unsigned char *buf,
                                    size_t *len,
                                    size_t *offset);
functions.description: Serialize a single resource’s link-format description into buf, supporting Block2-style partial output via offset. Returns a status word where the lower 28 bits are the number of bytes output; COAP_PRINT_STATUS_ERROR signals error, COAP_PRINT_STATUS_TRUNC indicates truncation.
requirements: resource must be a valid resource to describe.
buf must point to a valid output buffer; len must be initialized to the buffer’s maximum length on input and is set to the number of bytes written on success.
offset provides the starting offset within the full description and is updated as output is consumed (Block2 support).

Caller must inspect the returned coap_print_status_t: if COAP_PRINT_STATUS_ERROR is set, an error occurred; otherwise the lower 28 bits give the number of bytes written; COAP_PRINT_STATUS_TRUNC indicates truncation.

functions.name: coap_print_wellknown
functions.signature:
COAP_API coap_print_status_t coap_print_wellknown(coap_context_t *context,
                                                  unsigned char *buf,
                                                  size_t *buflen,
                                                  size_t offset,
                                                  const coap_string_t *query_filter);
functions.description: Generate the aggregate /.well-known/core link-format for all resources in the context into buf, optionally filtered by a link-format query. Returns a status word with length and flags similar to coap_print_link().
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t containing the resource map.
buf must point to a valid output buffer; buflen must be initialized to buf’s capacity on input and is set to the number of bytes written on return.
offset is the starting byte offset for output to support block-wise transfers; it is adjusted internally as characters are processed.
query_filter may be NULL or a valid coap_string_t with a link-format filter query.
Caller must check the returned coap_print_status_t for COAP_PRINT_STATUS_ERROR and COAP_PRINT_STATUS_TRUNC; the lower 28 bits are the number of bytes written when no error.

functions.name: coap_resource_set_dirty
functions.signature:
COAP_DEPRECATED COAP_API int coap_resource_set_dirty(coap_resource_t *r,
                                                     const coap_string_t *query);
functions.description: Deprecated: mark a resource as needing observer notification (dirty). Use coap_resource_notify_observers() instead. Returns an int status (non-specified here).
requirements: r must be a valid coap_resource_t.
query may be NULL or a valid coap_string_t representing a query for selective notifications.
Function is deprecated; new code should migrate to coap_resource_notify_observers().
Return value semantics are not documented here; callers must handle potential nonzero/zero status appropriately.

functions.name: coap_session_reference
functions.description: Increment the reference counter for a CoAP session and return the same session pointer. Use to hold an extra reference to a session object.
requirements: session must be a valid, initialized coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_release
functions.description: Decrement the session's reference counter; the session may be deleted as a result, so it must not be used after this call if the count reaches zero.
requirements: session must be a valid, initialized coap_session_t pointer.
Caller must not access session after this call if it caused deletion (i.e., if reference count reached zero).

functions.name: coap_session_disconnected
functions.description: Notify the session that it has failed/disconnected, causing cleanup of outstanding or queued transmissions, observations, etc.
requirements: session must be a valid, initialized coap_session_t pointer.
reason must be a valid coap_nack_reason_t value.

functions.name: coap_session_set_app_data
functions.description: Deprecated. Store application-specific data pointer in the session, overwriting any previously stored value. Prefer coap_session_set_app_data2() for lifetime management.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
data may be NULL to clear.
Caller is responsible for managing the lifetime of any previously stored data as this API does not return it or provide a free callback.

functions.name: coap_session_get_app_data
functions.description: Return the application-specific data previously stored with coap_session_set_app_data() or coap_session_set_app_data2(), or NULL if none.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_set_app_data2
functions.description: Store application-specific data in the session and optionally provide a callback to free it when the session is deleted. Returns the previously stored data pointer (if any).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
data may be NULL to clear the previous data.
If callback is provided, it must be safe to call during session deletion with the stored data pointer.
Caller is responsible for freeing any returned (previous) data as appropriate.

functions.name: coap_session_get_addr_remote
functions.description: Get the remote (peer) IP address and port associated with the session. For clients, after a multicast request it may return the responding IP until the next coap_send() restores the multicast address.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_addr_mcast
functions.description: Get the remote multicast IP address and port for the session if the original target was multicast. Only available for a client session; returns NULL otherwise or on failure.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
Only meaningful for client sessions; may return NULL for non-multicast sessions.

functions.name: coap_session_get_addr_local
functions.description: Get the local IP address and port used by the session.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_proto
functions.description: Return the protocol used by the session (e.g., UDP, DTLS, TCP, TLS, WS, WSS).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_type
functions.description: Return the session type (client, server, hello, or none).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_state
functions.description: Return the current session state (e.g., CONNECTING, HANDSHAKE, CSM, ESTABLISHED).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_endpoint
functions.description: Return the endpoint associated with the session, or NULL on error.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_ifindex
functions.description: Return the interface index used by the session, or -1 on error.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_get_tls
functions.description: Return the underlying TLS/DTLS library-specific session pointer and set tls_lib to the library type. Returns NULL if TLS is not set up. TLS type depends on the build (OpenSSL, GnuTLS, Mbed TLS, TinyDTLS).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
tls_lib must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the library type.

functions.name: coap_session_get_context
functions.description: Return the libcoap context associated with the session.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_session_set_type_client
functions.description: Convert a server-type session to a client-type session (used in call-home scenarios). On success, increments the session reference count; a later coap_session_release() that brings the count to zero will free the session. DTLS server sessions cannot be converted before ClientHello; call after COAP_EVENT_SERVER_SESSION_CONNECTED.
requirements: session must currently be of type COAP_SESSION_TYPE_SERVER.
For DTLS server sessions, must not be called before the ClientHello is seen; call after receiving COAP_EVENT_SERVER_SESSION_CONNECTED.
Caller must handle increased reference count on success (balance with coap_session_release).

functions.name: coap_session_set_type_server
functions.description: Convert a client-type session to a server-type session (used in call-home flows). On success, decrements the reference count so the session behaves like a normal server session that may idle timeout. Should be called immediately after a successful coap_new_client_session*() call.
requirements: session must currently be of type COAP_SESSION_TYPE_CLIENT.
Should be called immediately after a successful coap_new_client_session*() function.
Caller must account for the reference count decrement on success.

functions.name: coap_session_set_mtu
functions.description: Set the session MTU (maximum message size that can be sent), excluding IP and UDP overhead.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
mtu must represent the intended maximum application-layer payload size excluding IP/UDP overhead. Exact range is not specified.

functions.name: coap_session_max_pdu_size
functions.description: Return the maximum acceptable PDU size for the session, not including the CoAP header but including the token.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_new_client_session
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session(coap_context_t *ctx, const coap_address_t *local_if, const coap_address_t *server, coap_proto_t proto);
functions.description: Create a new client session to the specified server using the given protocol. Returns a new session or NULL on failure. Release with coap_session_release().
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
local_if may be NULL to let the OS choose a local interface; if specified, its port should be 0 to auto-select a free port.
server must be a valid address; if server port is 0, the protocol default port is used.
proto must be a valid coap_proto_t.
Caller must call coap_session_release() to free the session when done.

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_psk
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session_psk(coap_context_t *ctx, const coap_address_t *local_if, const coap_address_t *server, coap_proto_t proto, const char *identity, const uint8_t *key, unsigned key_len);
functions.description: Deprecated. Create a new client session with PSK credentials. Prefer coap_new_client_session_psk2(). Returns a new session or NULL on failure. Release with coap_session_release().
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
local_if may be NULL; if specified, its port should be 0 for auto-selection.
server must be a valid address; if server port is 0, the protocol default port is used.
proto must be a valid coap_proto_t.
identity must point to the PSK client identity string (NULL handling not specified).
key must point to the PSK shared key; key_len specifies its length.
Caller must call coap_session_release() to free the session when done.

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_psk2
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session_psk2(coap_context_t *ctx, const coap_address_t *local_if, const coap_address_t *server, coap_proto_t proto, coap_dtls_cpsk_t *setup_data);
functions.description: Create a new client session with PSK credentials specified by setup_data. Returns a new session or NULL on failure. Release with coap_session_release().
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
local_if may be NULL; if specified, its port should be 0 for auto-selection.
server must be a valid address; if server port is 0, the protocol default port is used.
proto must be a valid coap_proto_t.
setup_data must be a valid coap_dtls_cpsk_t pointer with appropriate PSK parameters initialized.
Caller must call coap_session_release() to free the session when done.

functions.name: coap_session_get_psk_hint
functions.description: Return the server session’s current Identity Hint (PSK) or NULL if unavailable.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
Only meaningful when PSK is in use on a server session.

functions.name: coap_session_get_psk_identity
functions.description: Return the server session’s current PSK identity or NULL if unavailable.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
Only meaningful when PSK is in use.

functions.name: coap_session_get_psk_key
functions.description: Return the session’s current pre-shared key (PSK) or NULL if unavailable.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
Only meaningful when PSK is in use.

functions.name: coap_new_client_session_pki
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_session_t *coap_new_client_session_pki(coap_context_t *ctx, const coap_address_t *local_if, const coap_address_t *server, coap_proto_t proto, coap_dtls_pki_t *setup_data);
functions.description: Create a new client session using PKI (certificate-based) credentials specified in setup_data. Returns a new session or NULL on failure. Release with coap_session_release().
requirements: ctx must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
local_if may be NULL; if specified, its port should be 0 for auto-selection.
server must be a valid address; if server port is 0, the protocol default port is used.
proto must be a valid coap_proto_t.
setup_data must be a valid coap_dtls_pki_t pointer with necessary PKI parameters initialized.
Caller must call coap_session_release() to free the session when done.

functions.name: coap_session_init_token
functions.signature: void coap_session_init_token(coap_session_t *session, size_t length, const uint8_t *token);
functions.description: Initialize the session’s token value as a starting point for future tokens.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
length must be between 0 and 8 bytes inclusive.
token must point to at least length bytes (ignored if length is 0).

functions.name: coap_session_new_token
functions.description: Generate a new token for use. Updates length with the token length and writes the token bytes into the provided 8-byte buffer.
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.
length must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive the token length.
token must point to a buffer of at least 8 bytes.

functions.name: coap_session_str
functions.description: Return a human-readable description string for the session (for logging/diagnostics).
requirements: session must be a valid coap_session_t pointer.

functions.name: coap_new_endpoint
functions.signature: COAP_API coap_endpoint_t *coap_new_endpoint(coap_context_t *context, const coap_address_t *listen_addr, coap_proto_t proto);
functions.description: Create a new endpoint for communicating with peers. If listen_addr is NULL, no incoming requests are accepted and a random endpoint is used. Returns the endpoint or NULL on failure.
requirements: context must be a valid coap_context_t pointer.
listen_addr may be NULL; if non-NULL, it specifies the address the endpoint listens on or originates from.
proto must be a valid coap_proto_t.
Caller should free the endpoint with coap_free_endpoint() when done.

functions.name: coap_endpoint_set_default_mtu
functions.description: Set the endpoint’s default MTU (maximum message size that can be sent), excluding IP and UDP overhead.
requirements: endpoint must be a valid coap_endpoint_t pointer.
mtu is an unsigned value representing the application-layer max size; exact range not specified.

functions.name: coap_free_endpoint
functions.description: Release an endpoint and all associated structures.

The extra byte typically allows space for a terminating NUL if the data is used as a C string.
requirements: Caller must free the returned object with coap_delete_string() when no longer needed.
On success, caller must initialize the string’s contents and set a valid length before use.
If used as a C string, ensure any terminator fits within the allocated size+1 (inferred from documentation).
Do not assume size == length; caller is responsible for setting length appropriately.
On error, the function returns NULL and no object is allocated.

functions.name: coap_delete_string
functions.description: Frees a coap_string_t and any memory it owns.
requirements: string must be a valid pointer previously returned by coap_new_string() and not already freed.
Behavior for NULL is not documented; pass a non-NULL pointer.
Do not use the string pointer after calling this function.

functions.name: coap_new_str_const
functions.description: Creates a new immutable (const) CoAP string object, copying size bytes from data into internal storage. The object must be released with coap_delete_str_const().
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of initialized memory that can be read until the copy completes.
If size > 0, data must be non-NULL; if size == 0, data may be NULL (inferred as typical use; not explicitly stated).
Caller must free the returned object with coap_delete_str_const() when no longer needed.
On error, returns NULL and no object is allocated.

functions.name: coap_delete_str_const
functions.description: Frees a coap_str_const_t and any memory it owns.
requirements: string must be a valid pointer previously returned by coap_new_str_const() and not already freed.
Behavior for NULL is not documented; pass a non-NULL pointer.
Do not use the pointer after calling this function.

functions.description: Allocates and returns a new mutable CoAP binary object with at least size bytes of storage for binary data. Caller must initialize the returned object’s fields (e.g., length and data contents) before use and release it with coap_delete_binary().
requirements: Caller must free the returned object with coap_delete_binary() when no longer needed.

functions.description: Frees a coap_binary_t and any memory it owns.
requirements: binary must be a valid pointer previously returned by coap_new_binary() or coap_resize_binary() and not already freed.

functions.name: coap_resize_binary
